question_content: pA developer runs an AWS CLI command on an Amazon EC2 instance. However, the command fails with the following response:/pp/ppspan style="font-family: Courier New"A client error (UnauthorizedOperation) occurred when calling the RunInstances operation: You are not authorized to perform this operation. Encoded authorization failure message: mVqaktia1h2cDhtVG90THBhK216SG9reldscThOcHlqeXo3M3ZJU3NZMVg4SWVUQVNvZVUrIGltRDYrSDZ2QWdFNXhYQk5MQWw4Qmg5S3QzbU16S2RDM2VjZVFLV09KTlRiZjNSU3VFSXdobnpiYlo5UTJRUkNSZy81SjdiTDZlZzFhdFkwRDVqeFV5SWRucENEe/span/ppHow can the developer decode the response in the encoded portion of the message?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the AWS Support create-case command to create a support ticket. Send the encoded authorization failure message content.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Some AWS operations return an encoded authorization message. When you receive an encoded message, the decode-authorization-message command can help you decode additional information about the authorization status of a request from the encoded message that is returned in response to an AWS request. Because the developer can resolve this issue, there is no need to contact AWS Support./ppFor more information about how to decode an authorization message, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/sts/decode-authorization-message.html"decode-authorization-message.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) decrypt--ciphertext-blob command to decode the contents of the response.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The AWS KMS decrypt command decrypts ciphertext that was encrypted by an AWS KMS key. AWS KMS is not relevant to this scenario because the contents are not encrypted. The contents are encoded./ppFor more information about the decrypt command, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/kms/decrypt.html"decrypt.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the Amazon S3 describe-default-encryption-configuration command to decode the contents of the response.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The describe-default-encryption-configuration command retrieves information about the default encryption configuration for the AWS account. The contents in this scenario are not encrypted. The contents are encoded./ppFor more information about the default encryption configuration, see href="https://awscli.amazonaws.com/v2/documentation/api/latest/reference/iotsitewise/describe-default-encryption-configuration.html"describe-default-encryption-configuration.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) decode-authorization-message command to decode the contents of the response.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Certain AWS operations return an encoded authorization message. When you receive an encoded message, the AWS STS decode-authorization-message command can help you decode additional information about the authorization status of a request from an encoded message that is returned in response to an AWS request./ppFor more information about how to decode an authorization message, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/sts/decode-authorization-message.html"decode-authorization-message.

question_content: pAn AWS Elastic Beanstalk application needs to be deployed in multiple AWS Regions and requires a different Amazon Machine Image (AMI) in each Region./ppWhich AWS CloudFormation template key can be used to specify the correct AMI for each Region?

answer_choices.choice_content: pParameters
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Parameters give you the ability to input custom values to your CloudFormation template. Parameters do not map values to different Regions. /ppFor more information about parameters, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/parameters-section-structure.html"Parameters.

answer_choices.choice_content: pOutputs
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Outputs can export selected values from the CloudFormation stack. You can import the values into other stacks or display the values after you create or update a stack. You would not use outputs to specify Regional differences. /ppFor more information about outputs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/outputs-section-structure.html"Outputs.

answer_choices.choice_content: pMappings
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The CloudFormation mappings section matches a key to a corresponding set of named values. You can use mappings to specify the AMI ID for each Region. /ppFor more information about mappings, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/mappings-section-structure.html"Mappings.

answer_choices.choice_content: pResources
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The resources section defines the stack resources and properties. The resources section does not map Regional differences. /ppFor more information about resources, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/resources-section-structure.html"Resources.

question_content: pA company runs a discussion forum application on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The application stores data in Amazon DynamoDB. The company configured the table with provisioned capacity and Auto Scaling. The forum has a global user base. The traffic to the forum is uneven and sometimes spikes rapidly. Recently, users reported receiving intermittent errors on the forum. A developer inspected the application logs and found the following record:/ppspan style="font-family: Courier New"ProvisionedThroughputExceededException: 400 Bad Request/span/ppWhich action will resolve the issue that is causing the error?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the ECS cluster with Service Auto Scaling.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You would not resolve the Dynamo DB capacity issue by implementing Service Auto Scaling on the ECS cluster./ppFor more information about ECS Service Auto Scaling, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html"Service auto scaling.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement DynamoDB global tables.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Global tables would replicate the data across multiple tables in multiple Regions. This solution would not resolve the DynamoDB capacity issue because all the requests are coming from the same ECS cluster in a single Region./ppFor more information about DynamoDB global tables, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html"Global tables - multi-Region replication for DynamoDB.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpdate the DynamoDB table to use on-demand mode.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. If you update the table to use DynamoDB on-demand mode, you will ensure that the table can serve requests when workloads are uneven or spike rapidly./ppFor more information about DynamoDB on-demand mode, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.ReadWriteCapacityMode.html#HowItWorks.OnDemand"On-demand mode.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the ECS cluster to run more tasks.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You would not resolve the DynamoDB capacity issue by increasing the number of tasks that are running on the ECS cluster./ppFor more information about sizing ECS tasks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task_definitions.html"Amazon ECS task definitions.

question_content: pA company creates an online platform that uses an Amazon S3 bucket to give users the ability to upload and share videos. The company has integrated the platform with a mobile app that gives users the ability to record and immediately upload videos. A user is unable to upload videos and submits a support ticket for the issue. The company discovers the following error message related to the user's multiple upload attempts:/ppspan style="font-family: Courier New"EntityTooLarge: Your proposed upload exceeds the maximum allowed size./span/ppWhich solution will prevent the issue in any future upload attempts?

answer_choices.choice_content: pIncrease the maximum size for uploads for the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. There is no way to control the maximum size of an upload to an S3 bucket./ppFor more information about available settings for S3 buckets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingBucket.html#bucket-config-options-intro"Bucket configuration options.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement multipart upload logic on the mobile app.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The file size exceeded the maximum upload size limit for a single put operation. You can use multipart uploads in Amazon S3 to upload larger files./ppFor more information about multipart uploads in Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpuoverview.html"Uploading and copying objects using multipart upload.

answer_choices.choice_content: pIncrease the maximum capacity for the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. S3 buckets have unlimited capacity. S3 bucket capacity is not configurable./ppFor more information about available settings for S3 buckets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingBucket.html#bucket-config-options-intro"Bucket configuration options.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImplement S3 Transfer Acceleration on the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Transfer Acceleration can speed up transfers to S3 buckets. However, Transfer Acceleration would not overcome the single put upload limit for S3 buckets./ppFor more information about Transfer Acceleration, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/transfer-acceleration.html"Configuring fast, secure file transfers using Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration.

question_content: pA developer created an automated pipeline in AWS CodePipeline 6 months ago. The pipeline follows these stages:/pol  listrongSource/strongCommit code to AWS CodeCommit./li  listrongBuild/strongPerform a Docker build by using AWS CodeBuild. Write Docker images to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR)./li  listrongTest/strongLaunch an Amazon EC2 instance as a test environment. Run an image from Amazon ECR on the EC2 instance. Perform tests./li  listrongDeploy/strongDeploy the image to the production Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster by using AWS CodeDeploy./li/olpRecently, the CodeDeploy deployments began failing in Stage 4. The deployments are unable to perform rollbacks. The developer must minimize the number of failures that reach production without slowing down the pipeline./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd a human review and approval stage between Stage 3 and Stage 4.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The automated pipeline was fully functional until recently. A human review and approval stage will slow down deployments and increase the number of human errors./ppFor more information about continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) best practices, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/practicing-continuous-integration-continuous-delivery/summary-of-best-practices.html"Summary of best practices.

answer_choices.choice_content: pPerform a more comprehensive test before Stage 2 by adding a test for the CodeCommit trigger in Stage 1.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A CodeCommit trigger test is designed to test the triggers from CodeDeploy. A trigger test does not run on the code itself. This process will not improve the code quality or identify the potential failures before production./ppFor more information about CodeCommit trigger tests, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-notify-test.html"Test triggers for an AWS CodeCommit repository.

answer_choices.choice_content: pReplace Stage 4 with a manual deployment until the developer can add more quality tests to the automation.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The automated pipeline was fully functional until recently. A manual deployment will slow down deployments and increase the number of human errors./ppFor more information about continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) best practices, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/practicing-continuous-integration-continuous-delivery/summary-of-best-practices.html"Summary of best practices.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify Stage 3 so that it uses Amazon ECS and CodeDeploy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use CodeDeploy in the test and production environments to improve consistency. If the deployment architecture varies from the test environment to the production environment, you would be unable to fully duplicate all possible problems before deploying to production, including problems with the deployment itself. Without consistency between the test and production environments, tests cannot be fully reliable. If you perform the deployment by using Amazon ECS in the test environment in the same way that you perform the deployment in the production environment, you can test both the deployment methodology and configuration./ppFor more information about continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) best practices, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/practicing-continuous-integration-continuous-delivery/summary-of-best-practices.html" style="color: rgb(136, 136, 204); text-decoration-line: underline;"Summary of best practices. /ppFor more information about a similar architecture, see href="https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/containers/developing-twelve-factor-apps-using-amazon-ecs-and-aws-fargate/"Developing Twelve-Factor Apps using Amazon ECS and AWS Fargate. /ppFor more information about ECS deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/tutorial-ecs-deployment.html"Tutorial: Deploy an Amazon ECS service.

question_content: pAn application consists of an Amazon API Gateway REST API that invokes an AWS Lambda function based on a POST method. The Lambda function often fails because of a call to a third-party API inside the function code. There is a requirement to retry failures within a few hours./p	pA developer needs to improve the design to handle exceptions better. The application must have the ability to retry for an amount of time that exceeds the Lambda function's timeout period./p	pWhich solution meets these requirements?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a second Lambda function to handle exceptions. Invoke the original function with exponential backoff and retry logic. Configure API Gateway to invoke the new function instead of the original function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. It is possible to synchronously invoke a Lambda function from another Lambda function. However, the new Lambda function must wait until the original function has finished. The new function is still bound by the maximum timeout value./ppFor more information about Lambda timeout, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/runtimes-context.html"AWS Lambda Execution Environment.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Step Functions state machine. Create a task state that calls the original function with a retry. Set the BackoffRate and maxAttempts values. Configure API Gateway to start the state machine instead of to invoke the original Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use Step Functions to create complex workflows, including tasks that invoke Lambda functions. Standard workflows can be long-lived and can include tasks with retriers that retry a failed task. You can start a state machine from API Gateway REST API by using the POST method./ppFor more information about how to start a state machine from API Gateway, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/tutorial-api-gateway.html"Creating a Step Functions API Using API Gateway. /ppFor more information about how to retry errors in state machines, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/concepts-error-handling.html"Error Handling in Step Functions.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a Lambda external extension that handles exceptions as necessary. Remove the third-party API call from the original function. Register the extension with the original function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use Lambda extensions to integrate Lambda with your preferred tools for monitoring, observation, security, and governance. An external extension runs as an independent process in the runtime environment and can continue to run after the function invocation is fully processed. However, the Lambda timeout applies to the entire duration of the function and all its extensions. You cannot use extensions to circumvent the maximum timeout value for a Lambda function./ppFor more information about Lambda extensions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/runtimes-extensions-api.html"Lambda Extensions API. /ppFor more information about Lambda timeout, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/runtimes-context.html"AWS Lambda Execution Environment.

answer_choices.choice_content: pBuild a Lambda layer with a library of code that handles exceptions as necessary. Remove the third-party API call from the original function. Configure the original Lambda function to call the code in the library.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The code that is called within a Lambda layer is run in the same runtime context as the Lambda function. The call on the code counts toward the same timeout value. You cannot use layers to circumvent the maximum timeout value for a Lambda function./ppFor more information about Lambda layers, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-concepts.html#gettingstarted-concepts-layer"Layer. /ppFor more information about Lambda timeout, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/runtimes-context.html"AWS Lambda Execution Environment.

question_content: pA developer uses the AWS SDK for Java to put many records into an Amazon Kinesis data stream by using the PutRecord API call. The developer tracks a significant portion of CPU and network usage back to this single call. The developer must optimize the code to reduce resource usage and increase throughput./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCall the PutRecord API asynchronously in a background thread by using the SDK for Java.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A solution that moves the PutRecord API call to a background thread can potentially speed up a foreground thread, but this solution will not reduce network traffic or CPU usage. This solution will not change the number of times the calls are made or the amount of CPU and network resources required to make each call. Additional threading might increase CPU usage./ppFor more information about the PutRecord API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecord.html"PutRecord.

answer_choices.choice_content: pGather groups of records and call the PutRecords API by using the SDK for Java.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Each PutRecords API call can support many records, up to a size limit for the entire request. This support greatly increases throughput./ppFor more information about the PutRecords API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecords.html"PutRecords.

answer_choices.choice_content: pPut records in a background thread asynchronously by using the Kinesis Client Library (KCL).
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The KCL helps consume and process data from a Kinesis data stream by handling shard-to-worker relationships. However, the KCL does not address producer issues. Also, the KCL does not have the ability to put records into the stream./ppFor more information about the KCL, see ua target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/shared-throughput-kcl-consumers.html"Using the Kinesis Client Library/a/u.

answer_choices.choice_content: pGather groups of records and put the groups into the data stream by using the Kinesis Client Library (KCL).
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The KCL helps consume and process data from a Kinesis data stream by handling shard-to-worker relationships. However, the KCL does not address producer issues. Also, the KCL does not have the ability to put records into the stream./ppFor more information about the KCL, see ua target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/shared-throughput-kcl-consumers.html"Using the Kinesis Client Library/a/u.

question_content: pA development team at an ecommerce company uses an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to store submitted orders. The team writes an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances. The application reads orders from the SQS queue and writes the data to a relational database. Cases of duplicate orders are discovered daily in the database./p	pWhich actions will resolve the issue with duplicate orders? (Select TWO.)/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pIncrease the maximum number of messages on the ReceiveMessage API call beyond the current batch size of messages received in one call.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The maximum number of messages controls the batch size of messages received in one call. Changing this value would not affect the duplicate orders observed in the database./ppFor more information about ReceiveMessage, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_ReceiveMessage.html"ReceiveMessage.

answer_choices.choice_content: pIncrease the message's visibility timeout on the ReceiveMessage API call to beyond what the longest transaction takes to process.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. If the visibility timeout expires before the message is processed and deleted, another consumer could retrieve the message and process it again. This process would create duplicate information on the database. To prevent the duplications, AWS recommends setting the visibility timeout to a safe threshold, which is the maximum time that it takes the application to process and delete a message from the queue./ppFor more information about Amazon SQS visibility timeout, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-visibility-timeout.html"Amazon SQS Visibility Timeout.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUpdate the application so that it verifies that a message is not a duplicate before writing the data to the database.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Developers should design each application so that it does not create duplicates when processing the same message more than once. In this case, the database could be checked to see if another order for the same amount was already sent by a customer on the same day. If there is another order, ignore it or delete the duplicate.  /ppFor more information about at-least-once delivery, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html#standard-queues-at-least-once-delivery"At-least-once delivery.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet the wait time in seconds to a non-zero value on the ReceiveMessage API call.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A wait time in seconds value between 0 and 20 establishes long polling, which is a very useful feature when reducing the number of empty responses. Changing this value would not affect the duplicate orders observed in the database. /ppFor more information about long polling, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-short-and-long-polling.html"Amazon SQS short and long polling.

answer_choices.choice_content: pProvide a unique message group ID for each message with the SendMessage API call.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Setting a unique message group ID for each message helps the queue's throughput and latency at the expense of ordering. Changing the ID value would not affect the duplicate orders observed in the database./ppFor more information about processing duplicates, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/using-messagegroupid-property.html#avoding-processing-duplicates-in-multiple-producer-consumer-system"Avoiding processing duplicates in a multiple-producer/consumer system.

question_content: pAn e-commerce company must select a database to store product data for several million products. The company must notify three separate systems whenever product data changes. The company has already established an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with a subscription for each system. The company must notify the SNS topic as soon as product data changes in the database./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pStore product data in an Amazon RDS database instance that runs PostgreSQL. Create a database trigger to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Write code to send each change event to each SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An RDS database that runs PostgreSQL can hold several million product records. The database can send a notification whenever a change occurs. However, with the exception of Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition, a database notification has no way to invoke a Lambda function./ppFor more information about how to invoke a Lambda function, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-invocation.html"Invoking Lambda functions.

answer_choices.choice_content: pStore product data in an Amazon RDS database instance that runs PostgreSQL. Create a Lambda function that Amazon EventBridge will launch on a set schedule. Write code to scan the database for recent changes. Send each change event to each SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An RDS database that runs PostgreSQL can hold several million product records. You can run a Lambda function on a schedule. A Lambda function can connect to and query a relational database. However, you would not detect changes as soon as they occur by occasionally querying a database table to look for changes. A change notification could be delayed by the time of the polling interval./ppFor more information about how to run a Lambda function on a schedule, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/events/RunLambdaSchedule.html"Tutorial: Schedule AWS Lambda Functions Using CloudWatch Events.

answer_choices.choice_content: pStore product data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Define a DynamoDB stream on the table. Create a Lambda function with the stream as the event source. Write code to send each change event to each SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. DynamoDB can serve as a simple table structure. You can establish a DynamoDB stream on a table to capture changes that are made in the table. Lambda functions can use DynamoDB streams as an event source. Any Lambda function can contain code to send a notification to an SNS topic./ppFor more information about DynamoDB, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Introduction.html"What Is Amazon DynamoDB? /ppFor more information about DynamoDB streams, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html"Change data capture for DynamoDB Streams. /ppFor more information about DynamoDB streams as a Lambda event source, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.Lambda.html"DynamoDB Streams and AWS Lambda triggers. /ppFor more information about Amazon SNS subscribers, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-create-subscribe-endpoint-to-topic.html"Subscribing to an Amazon SNS topic.

answer_choices.choice_content: pStore product data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create a Lambda function that Amazon EventBridge will launch on a set schedule. Write code to scan the table to for recent changes. Send each change event to each SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Although it is possible to run a Lambda function on a schedule, you would not detect changes as soon as they occur by occasionally querying a database to look for changes. A change notification could be delayed by the time of the polling interval. It is not efficient to scan a multi-million item table to detect changes because the scan reads every item in the table. This solution would further delay the notifications./ppFor more information about how to scan DynamoDB tables, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_Scan.html"Scan.

question_content: pA developer deploys a custom application to three Amazon EC2 instances. The application processes messages from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue with default settings. When the developer runs a load test on the Amazon SQS queue, the developer discovers that the application processes many messages multiple times./ppHow can the developer ensure that the application processes each message exactly once?

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the SQS standard queue to an SQS FIFO queue.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot change the queue type after you create the queue./ppFor more information about how to create SQS queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-configure-create-queue.html"Creating an Amazon SQS queue (console).

answer_choices.choice_content: pProcess the messages on one EC2 instance instead of three instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution might still process the messages multiple times because of the at-least-once processing semantics that SQS standard queues support./ppFor more information about SQS standard queue at-least-once delivery, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/standard-queues.html"Amazon SQS Standard queues.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new SQS FIFO queue. Point the application to the new queue.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. SQS FIFO queues support exactly-once processing semantics./ppFor more information about SQS FIFO exactly-once processing semantics, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-queues-exactly-once-processing.html"Exactly-once processing.

answer_choices.choice_content: pIncrease the DelaySeconds value on the current SQS queue.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The DelaySeconds value of an SQS queue postpones the delivery of new messages to a queue. An increase to the DelaySeconds value will delay only the delivery to the queue. This solution would not influence the possibility of duplicate delivery in a standard SQS queue./ppFor more information about the SQS queue DelaySeconds value, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-delay-queues.html"Amazon SQS delay queues.

question_content: pA developer is building a web application that processes and tracks votes. A voting device submits the votes to an Amazon S3 bucket named DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET. The application needs to record the votes to an Amazon DynamoDB table named Example. The developer writes an AWS Lambda function to process the objects. The developer writes the following policy for the execution role of the Lambda function:/pspan style="font-family: Courier New"  p{/p  p    "Version": "2012-10-17",/p  p    "Statement": [/p  p        {/p  p            "Effect": "Allow",/p  p            "Action": [/p  p                "s3:GetObject",/p  p                "dynamodb:PutItem",/p  p                "dynamodb:UpdateItem"/p  p            ],/p  p            "Resource": [/p  p                "arn:aws:dynamodb:us-west-2:123456789012:table/Example",/p  p                "arn:aws:s3:::DOC-EXAMPLE-BUCKET/*"/p  p            ]/p  p        }/p  p    ]/p  p}/p/spanpThe developer ran a successful test on the Lambda function. question_content: pA developer has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. In addition to the default ALB health checks, the developer writes a custom script that will periodically determine an application-specific status for each EC2 instance. The developer wants to schedule the script to run every 10 minutes./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeploy a NAT gateway in front of the EC2 instances. Run the script as a health check on the NAT gateway every 10 minutes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. It is possible to use a NAT gateway so that instances in a private subnet can connect to services outside a VPC. However, NAT gateways do not support any kind of health checks./ppFor more information about NAT gateways, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html"NAT gateways.

You can invoke Lambda functions on a schedule by using EventBridge./ppFor more information about how to connect a Lambda function to a VPC, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-vpc.html"Configuring a Lambda function to access resources in a VPC./ppFor more information about how to invoke Lambda functions by using EventBridge, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-run-lambda-schedule.html"Tutorial: Schedule AWS Lambda functions using EventBridge.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeploy the script on an AWS Lambda function behind a VPC-connected API gateway. Query the API gateway every 10 minutes.

However, the company requires the opposite; the Lambda function must be able to connect to check the status of the EC2 instances./ppFor more information about API gateways, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/welcome.html"What Is Amazon API Gateway?/ppFor more information about how to connect a Lambda function to a VPC, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-vpc.html"Configuring a Lambda function to access resources in a VPC.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeploy the script as a custom health check on the ALB to override the default health check. Set the health check period to 10 minutes.

question_content: pA research company has a website that is used once each day to perform scientific calculations based on inputs that are submitted through a webpage. question_content: pA developer has an Amazon API Gateway API that is integrated with an AWS Lambda function. The function reads and writes to a relational database. question_content: pA developer is updating an application deployed on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. The new version is incompatible with the old version. question_content: pA developer needs to migrate an existing web application to AWS. The application will run on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. question_content: pA company integrated a third-party online auction application into the company's website to sell rare products. The third party created the auction application by using serverless technologies. The application stores data in Amazon DynamoDB. The DynamoDB tables are in the company's AWS account and under the control of the company's development team. The development team wants to create a new application to add custom functionality that will apply to newly placed bids in the auction application. However, the team must meet the following requirements:  /pul    liThe team cannot change any of the third-party auction application code. /li    liThe new application must be serverless. /li    liThe new application must invoke the new functionality as soon as a user places a bid./li  /ul  Which solution will meet these requirements?/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pCode a new application that polls the DynamoDB table every minute for bids. Apply the custom functionality when the new application finds new bids. Deploy the new application on a single Amazon EC2 instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Polling for events such as a newly placed bid can cause a lag between the event and when the application discovers the event and can react. Event-driven architectures can better respond to events as soon as they happen./ppFor more information about event-driven architectures, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/operatorguide/event-driven-benefits.html"The benefits of event-driven architectures.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCode a new application that polls the DynamoDB table every minute for bids. Apply the new functionality when the new application finds new bids. Package the new code as a Docker image. Deploy the new application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Polling for events such as a newly placed bid can cause a lag between the event and when the application discovers the event and can react. Event-driven architectures can better respond to events as soon as they happen./ppFor more information about event-driven architectures, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/operatorguide/event-driven-benefits.html"The benefits of event-driven architectures.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the DynamoDB table to use DynamoDB Streams. Create an AWS Lambda function with the DynamoDB stream as the event source. Code the Lambda function to apply the new functionality when the stream message corresponds to a newly placed bid.
