DynamoDB Streams stores this information in a log for up to 24 hours. Applications can access this log and view the data items as the items appeared before and after they were modified in near real time (NRT). A Lambda function is a serverless solution to send messages from a DynamoDB stream./ppFor more information about DynamoDB streams, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.html"Change data capture for DynamoDB Streams./ppFor more information about how to use Lambda with DynamoDB Streams, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Streams.Lambda.html"DynamoDB Streams and AWS Lambda triggers.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a delivery stream in Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Configure the delivery stream to read changes from the DynamoDB table. Build a new application to read from the delivery stream and package the new application as a Docker image. Deploy the new application in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A DynamoDB table cannot be the direct producer of messages for Kinesis Data Firehose. To get messages into the stream, the company would need to build another application that would find the changes in DynamoDB and write them to the delivery stream./ppFor more information about how to write to Kinesis Data Firehose, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/basic-write.html"Sending Data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose Delivery Stream.

question_content: pA company is building an application to track athlete performance using an Amazon DynamoDB table. The table has already been created, and each item in the table is identified by a partition key (user_id) and a sort key (sport_name). The table design is shown below:/ppPartition Key: span style="font-family: Courier New"user_id/span/ppSort Key: span style="font-family: Courier New"sport_name/span/ppAttributes: span style="font-family: Courier New"score/span/pp                 span style="font-family: Courier New"score_datetime/span/ppem(Note: Not all table attributes are shown.)/em/ppA developer is asked to write a leaderboard application to display the top performers (user_id) based on the score for each sport_name./ppWhich process will allow the developer to extract results MOST efficiently from the DynamoDB table?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse a DynamoDB query operation with the key attributes of user_id and sport_name, and order the results based on the score attribute.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A DynamoDB query operation gives you the ability to retrieve data with a partition key and, optionally, a sort key. Because the partition key and the sort key do not include the score, you must scan the entire table to get a leaderboard of top performers. If possible, you should avoid scanning the entire table. Instead, a global secondary index efficiently retrieves the leaderboard./ppFor more information about the query operation in DynamoDB, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_Query.html"Query.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a global secondary index with a partition key of sport_name and a sort key of score, and get the results.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A global secondary index efficiently retrieves the leaderboard. You can create a global secondary index named leaderboard, with a partition key of sport_name and a sort key of score. The base table's primary key attributes are always projected into an index, so the user_id attribute is also present. Additionally, you can create a global secondary index after the table is already created./ppFor more information about global secondary indexes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GSI.html"Using Global Secondary Indexes in DynamoDB.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse a DynamoDB scan operation to retrieve scores and user_id based on sport_name, and order the results based on the score attribute.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A scan operation in DynamoDB reads every item in a table or a secondary index. To prevent performance issues or high workload costs, it is best practice not to scan large tables./ppFor more information about the scan operation in DynamoDB, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Scan.html"Working with Scans in DynamoDB.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a local secondary index with a primary key of sport_name and a sort key of score, and get the results based on the score attribute.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Local secondary indexes on a table are created only when the table is created. Because the table is already created, a local secondary index cannot be created./ppFor more information about local secondary indexes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/LSI.html"Local Secondary Indexes.

question_content: pA company has an ecommerce application that stores inventory data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Occasionally during price updates, some items are updated concurrently. This process generates some prices that are different from the prices that the company intended./ppWhich DynamoDB feature should a developer use to enforce consistency in the price update process?

answer_choices.choice_content: pAtomic counters
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An atomic counter is a numeric attribute that updates without interference to other requests. You can use an atomic counter to track page views or other use cases where overcounting or undercounting is tolerable./ppFor more information about atomic counters, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/WorkingWithItems.html#WorkingWithItems.AtomicCounters"Atomic Counters.

answer_choices.choice_content: pBatch operations
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Batch operations give you the ability to get or to update multiple items at the same time. However, batch operations do not ensure consistency of the operation. /ppFor more information about batch operations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/WorkingWithItems.html#WorkingWithItems.BatchOperations"Batch Operations.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConditional writes
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A conditional write succeeds only if the item attributes meet one or more expected conditions. Conditional writes are helpful when you want to ensure that an update succeeds only if an item currently has a specific value./ppFor more information about conditional writes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/WorkingWithItems.html#WorkingWithItems.ConditionalUpdate"Conditional Writes.

answer_choices.choice_content: pTTL
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A TTL value on a table gives you the ability to specify a per-item timestamp. DynamoDB will delete the items shortly after the TTL timestamp is met. /ppFor more information about TTL, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/TTL.html"Expiring Items by Using DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL).

question_content: pA developer must resolve user support tickets for a cross-platform client application. The application uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to cache content in front of an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The application uses Amazon Cognito for authentication, authorization, and user management. Users need the ability to access the same user data across multiple devices and platforms./ppWhich solution will help the developer meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon Cognito Sync client libraries on the client devices.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Amazon Cognito Sync is an AWS service that gives developers the ability to synchronize user profile data across mobile devices and the web./ppFor more information about how to sync application-related user data across devices, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-sync.html"Amazon Cognito Sync.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the ALB with sticky sessions.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The developer can use the ALB sticky session feature to allow the load balancer to bind a user's session to a specific target. This process will ensure that each device in use would access a single server. However, this process would not synchronize content across devices./ppFor more information about sticky sessions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/sticky-sessions.html"Sticky sessions for your Application Load Balancer.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an Amazon Route 53 alias record that points to the CloudFront distribution.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can create Amazon Route 53 alias records and point them to the CloudFront distribution to give the clients the ability to connect to the application through the custom domain when you use a custom domain name. However, this solution would not synchronize user data across devices./ppFor more information about Route 53, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-to-cloudfront-distribution.html"Routing traffic to an Amazon CloudFront distribution by using your domain name.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an AWS DataSync agent on the client devices.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. DataSync transfers data between on-premises storage systems and AWS storage services. You cannot use DataSync to synchronize user data across devices./ppFor more information about DataSync, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/what-is-datasync.html"What is AWS DataSync?

question_content: pA company uses the AWS SDK for JavaScript in the Browser to build a web application and then hosts the application on Amazon S3. The company wants the application to support 10,000 users concurrently. The company selects Amazon DynamoDB to store user preferences in a table. There is a requirement to uniquely identify users at any scale./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a user cookie. Attach an IAM role to the S3 bucket that hosts the application.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon S3 does not provide the ability to use a role to access other AWS services./ppFor more information about services that support the use of IAM roles, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.html"IAM roles.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an origin access control (OAC) to access the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use the OAC to restrict access to the S3 bucket from the public internet by ensuring that users access all content through a CloudFront distribution. However, you cannot use the OAC to identify users./ppFor more information about how to use the OAC feature to restrict access to Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/private-content-restricting-access-to-s3.html#private-content-restricting-access-to-s3-oai"Using an origin access control.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure and use Amazon Cognito. Access DynamoDB with the authenticated users.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use Amazon Cognito to identify users at scale. You can grant access to DynamoDB by using an identity credential provided by Amazon Cognito./ppFor more information about how to use Amazon Cognito to authenticate users in DynamoDB, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Cognito.Credentials.html"Configuring AWS credentials in your files using Amazon Cognito./ppFor more information about Amazon Cognito, including an implementation example, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-javascript/v3/developer-guide/loading-browser-credentials-cognito.html"Using Amazon Cognito Identity to authenticate users.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM user for each user. Use fine-grained access control on the DynamoDB table to control access.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. IAM policies make fine-grained access control possible in DynamoDB. However, IAM is not intended for application authentication or authorization. Because there are 10,000 users, this solution would exceed the quota for IAM users quickly./ppFor more information about fine-grained access control in DynamoDB, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/specifying-conditions.html"Using IAM policy conditions for fine-grained access control./ppFor more information about the limitations of using IAM to authenticate users at scale, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_iam-quotas.html"IAM and AWS STS quotas.

question_content: pA gaming company uses an Amazon Cognito user pool to allow users to sign into its mobile games. The company needs to add social identity providers (IdPs) to the user pool to simplify the way that users log into the games./p	pWhat information must the company provide to the Amazon Cognito user pool to add each social IdP?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe IdP URL, username, and password
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. OpenID providers require an app client ID and an app client secret. No username or password is exchanged during setup or use of an IdP./ppFor more information about how to add sign-in through a third party, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-identity-federation.html"Adding user pool sign-in through a third party.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) metadata document
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A SAML metadata document describes a SAML deployment. The deployment might include a SAML IdP or a SAML service provider. Social IdPs do not use SAML metadata documents. Social IdPs are based on OpenID./ppFor more information about how to add a SAML IdP to a user pool, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-managing-saml-idp-console.html"Creating and managing a SAML identity provider for a user pool (AWS Management Console).

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe access key ID and the secret access key of the user
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Social IdP do not use AWS credentials./ppFor more information about how to add sign-in through a third party, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-identity-federation.html"Adding user pool sign-in through a third party.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe app client ID and the app client secret
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Social IdPs are based on OpenID. All OpenID providers require the client application to register. The results of registration are an app client ID and an app client secret. Communications from the client application to the OpenID provider are expected to provide these values in each call./ppFor information about how to add a social IdP to a user pool, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-social-idp.html#cognito-user-pools-social-idp-step-2"Step 2: Add a social IdP to your user pool.

question_content: pA mobile app obtains an OpenID token by using a web identity provider's login process. The code needs AWS credentials to make a call to Amazon DynamoDB./ppHow can the code obtain AWS credentials?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an Amazon Cognito identity pool. Call the GetOpenIdToken API, then call the LookupDeveloperIdentity API.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The GetOpenIdToken API can obtain an OpenID token by using an Amazon Cognito ID. The scenario requires the opposite: given an OpenID token, acquire an Amazon Cognito ID, and then acquire AWS credentials. The LookupDeveloperIdentity API does not return credentials./ppFor more information about how to obtain AWS credentials by using an OpenID token, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/authentication-flow.html"Identity pools (federated identities) authentication flow./ppFor more information about the GetOpenIdToken API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognitoidentity/latest/APIReference/API_GetOpenIdToken.html"GetOpenIdToken./ppFor more information about the LookupDeveloperIdentity API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognitoidentity/latest/APIReference/API_LookupDeveloperIdentity.html"LookupDeveloperIdentity.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an Amazon Cognito user pool. Call the GetUser API, then call the InitiateAuth API.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon Cognito user pools provide user management, not AWS credentials. The GetUser API can obtain user attributes for a given access token. The InitiateAuth API can initiate an authorization flow. Neither of these calls will provide the necessary credentials./ppFor more information about the GetUser API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito-user-identity-pools/latest/APIReference/API_GetUser.html"GetUser./ppFor more information about the InitiateAuth API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito-user-identity-pools/latest/APIReference/API_InitiateAuth.html"InitiateAuth.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an Amazon Cognito identity pool. Call the GetId API, then call the GetCredentialsForIdentity API.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The GetId API is called with an OpenId token from a web identity provider and returns an Amazon Cognito ID. The GetCredentialsForIdentity API is called with an Amazon Cognito ID and returns temporary credentials. This flow is known as "enhanced (simplified) authflow," and it presumes that the identity pool, IAM roles, and external identity providers have all been configured./ppFor more information about how to obtain AWS credentials by using an OpenID token, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/authentication-flow.html"Identity pools (federated identities) authentication flow./ppFor more information about the GetId API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognitoidentity/latest/APIReference/API_GetId.html"GetId./ppFor more information about the GetCredentialsForIdentity API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognitoidentity/latest/APIReference/API_GetCredentialsForIdentity.html"GetCredentialsForIdentity.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an Amazon Cognito user pool. Call the GetUser API, then call the VerifySoftwareToken API.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon Cognito user pools provide user management, not AWS credentials. The GetUser API is used to obtain user attributes for a given access token. The VerifySoftwareToken API is used to validate a user's code for multi-factor authentication (MFA). Neither of these calls will provide the necessary credentials./ppFor more information about the GetUser API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito-user-identity-pools/latest/APIReference/API_GetUser.html"GetUser./ppFor more information about the VerifySoftwareToken API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito-user-identity-pools/latest/APIReference/API_VerifySoftwareToken.html"VerifySoftwareToken.

question_content: pA gaming company maintains a website that must display a list of the top 10 highest scores for a game. The company stores the top 10 list in Amazon DynamoDB. Users who access this page are not authenticated. The company must use the AWS SDK for JavaScript in the Browser to make the DynamoDB API call./ppWhich solution is the MOST secure way to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM user. Store the user's access key ID and secret access key in the website. Create the DynamoDB client object with these values.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An IAM user is associated with permanent credentials, not temporary credentials. A website, or any source code, should not contain long-term credential values./ppFor more information about best practices for AWS credential management, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/accounts/latest/reference/credentials-access-keys-best-practices.html%20"Best practices for managing AWS access keys.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM role. Store the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the role in the website. Create the DynamoDB client object with this value.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The DynamoDB client requires AWS security credentials. A role ARN is not a security credential./ppFor more information about the use of AWS security credentials, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-javascript/v3/developer-guide/setting-credentials.html"Setting credentials.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM role. Store the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the role in the website. Use the ARN to call the AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) AssumeRole API. Create the DynamoDB client object with the returned access key ID, secret access key, and security token.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The AssumeRole API requires AWS security credentials. A role ARN is not a security credential./ppFor more information about the AssumeRole API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRole.html"AssumeRole.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM role. Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool. Associate the role with unauthenticated identities. Create the DynamoDB client object with temporary credentials that the AWS.CognitoIdentityCredentials object returns.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An Amazon Cognito identity pool can grant unauthenticated users access to AWS services by using temporary credentials. The role's policies authorize calls made by using these temporary credentials./ppFor more information about Amazon Cognito identity pools, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-identity.html"Amazon Cognito identity pools (federated identities).

question_content: pA company designs a mobile app to run on AWS. The app will run on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances will run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. The app must securely access data that the company stores in Amazon DynamoDB./p	pWhich solution is MOST secure?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Cognito user pool for the mobile app users. Attach an IAM policy that has the required DynamoDB permissions to the user pool.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You could use a Cognito user pool for web identity federation. However, a Cognito user pool has no mechanism to provide the AWS credentials that are necessary to access DynamoDB or similar services./ppFor more information about Cognito user pools, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-identity-pools.html"Amazon Cognito user pools.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Lambda authorizer with the required DynamoDB permissions. Attach the Lambda authorizer to the Application Load Balancer.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot use a Lambda authorizer with the Application Load Balancer. Lambda authorizers are designed to be used with Amazon API Gateway./ppFor more information about the Lambda authorizers, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-use-lambda-authorizer.html"Use API Gateway Lambda authorizers.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM user for each mobile user. Attach an IAM policy that provides the required DynamoDB permissions to each IAM user.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. There is a limit for the maximum number of IAM users allowed in an account that would severely limit the number of possible users for the mobile app. More importantly, the number of permanent individual security credentials can be considered a security risk. For applications that run on EC2 instances, AWS recommends the use of temporary credentials through IAM roles./ppFor more information about IAM best practices, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html"Security best practices in IAM.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an IAM role. Attach a policy with the required DynamoDB permissions to the role. Configure the EC2 Auto Scaling launch template to attach the role to all EC2 instances.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. For applications that run on EC2 instances, AWS recommends the use of temporary credentials through IAM roles. You can configure the IAM roles for an EC2 Auto Scaling group through the launch template./ppFor more information about IAM best practices, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/best-practices.html"Security best practices in IAM./ppFor more information about how to set IAM roles in launch templates, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/us-iam-role.html"IAM role for applications that run on Amazon EC2 instances.

question_content: pA company has an application that must use Amazon Cognito identity pool attribute-based access control to limit user access to Amazon S3 objects by department. The company uses an Amazon Cognito user pool to authenticate all users. The company adds a "department" attribute and populates the attribute for each user. The company tags each S3 object with a corresponding "department" tag./ppHow can the company configure Amazon Cognito to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pDefine different IAM roles on the identity pool for each department. Select the role by using the role selector expression "$context.authorizer.claims.sub.department."
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. It is possible to associate multiple IAM roles with an identity pool's authentication mechanism. However, the role selection is based on a rule that specifies the user attribute/claim that is used to select the role. The syntax would follow the form "custom:department Equals X." Selection of one role over another is known as role-based access control, not attribute-based access control. The company requires attribute-based access control in this scenario./ppFor more information about role selection, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/role-based-access-control.html#using-rules-to-assign-roles-to-users"Using rule-based mapping to assign roles to users.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDefine different IAM roles on the user pool for each department. Select the role by using the role selector expression "$context.authorizer.claims.sub.department."
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. It is possible to associate IAM roles with user pool groups. The cognito:preferred_role claim can communicate these roles to an identity pool. However, a fixed algorithm performs the role selection. A role selection expression or rule does not perform the selection. Selection of one role over another is known as role-based access control, not attribute-based access control. The company requires attribute-based access control in this scenario./ppFor more information about role selection, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/role-based-access-control.html#using-tokens-to-assign-roles-to-users"Using tokens to assign roles to users.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDefine one IAM role on the identity pool. Associate the role with a policy that allows S3 permissions to any resource with the "s3:ExistingObjectTag/department": "${aws:PrincipalTag/department}" condition.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. In a process known as attribute-based access control, the principal's attributes from the user pool are used to allow or deny access to resources based on matching attributes. A single IAM role on the identity pool achieves this attribute-based access control. The user pool requires no information about roles, only a department attribute./ppFor more information about attribute-based access control, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/using-attributes-for-access-control-policy-example.html"Using attributes for access control policy example.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDefine one IAM role on the user pool. Associate the role with a policy that allows S3 permissions to any resource with the "s3:x-amz-metadata-directive": "${aws:PrincipalTag/department}" condition.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. It is possible to associate IAM roles with user pool groups. You cannot associate IAM roles with the overall user pool. This type of role could have a policy with a condition keyed on an attribute from the user pool. However, the given expression assesses this policy against the key's s3:x-amz-metadata-directive condition rather than a tag./ppFor more information about role selection, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/attributes-for-access-control.html"Using attributes for access control as a form of attribute-based access control.

question_content: pA new mobile app uses Amazon Cognito web identity federation. Immediately after a user logs in, the following error occurs:/p	pspan style="font-family: Courier New"AccessDenied -- Not authorized to perform sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity/span/p	pA developer determines that the Amazon Cognito configuration appears to be correct./p	pWhich of the following could be the cause of the error?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe app's developer incorrectly defined the authenticated principal role access policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The error indicates that the app did not allow the user to assume the role. This denial involves the trust policy. If the error were related to the access policy, the error would occur when the user attempted to log in by using the provided credentials for the role. An access policy error would not indicate AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS)./ppFor more information about trust permissions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/role-trust-and-permissions.html"Role trust and permissions. /ppFor more information about common IAM role mistakes, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/troubleshoot_roles.html#troubleshoot_roles_cant-assume-role"I can't assume a role.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe app could not confirm the user in the user pool.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. If the error were related to authentication, the process would not have progressed to the step where the user assumes a role. The step to assume a role comes after full authentication is successful./ppFor more information about Amazon Cognito authentication flow, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/authentication-flow.html"Identity pools (federated identities) authentication flow. /ppFor more information about authentication flow documentation for non-federated user pools, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/amazon-cognito-user-pools-authentication-flow.html"User pool authentication flow.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe app could not properly authenticate the user with the identity provider.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. If the error were related to authentication, the process would not have progressed to the step where the user assumes a role. The step to assume a role comes after full authentication is successful./ppFor more information about Amazon Cognito authentication flow, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/authentication-flow.html"Identity pools (federated identities) authentication flow./ppFor more information about authentication flow documentation for non-federated user pools, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/amazon-cognito-user-pools-authentication-flow.html"User pool authentication flow.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe app's developer incorrectly defined the authenticated principal role trust policy.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The trust policy likely does not contain the proper principal, action, or condition to fully grant access to the role to the user./ppFor more information about role and trust permissions related to Amazon Cognito, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/role-trust-and-permissions.html"Role trust and permissions./ppFor more information about common IAM role mistakes, see span style="text-decoration: underline;"span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/troubleshoot_roles.html#troubleshoot_roles_cant-assume-role"I can't assume a role/span.

question_content: pA company is designing a public upload platform on Amazon S3. Anyone should be able to upload data that is encrypted with a public key. Only the company should be able to decrypt the uploaded data. The company needs to use an asymmetric encryption key for this functionality./ppWhich feature can the company use to directly meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pServer-side encryption with customer-provided encryption keys (SSE-C)
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. SSE-C supports the use of symmetric keys. SSE-C does not support asymmetric keys./ppFor more information about S3 client-side encryption, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingClientSideEncryption.html"Protecting data using client-side encryption.

answer_choices.choice_content: pServer-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS)
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to create asymmetric keys. However, SSE-KMS supports symmetric keys, not asymmetric keys./ppFor more information about SSE-KMS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingKMSEncryption.html"Using server-side encryption with AWS Key Management Service (SSE-KMS).

answer_choices.choice_content: pClient-side encryption with customer-managed encryption keys
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Client-side encryption with customer-managed encryption keys allows you to select either symmetric or asymmetric keys./ppFor more information about S3 client-side encryption, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingClientSideEncryption.html"Protecting data using client-side encryption.

answer_choices.choice_content: pClient-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. S3 managed encryption keys are symmetric. You can use these keys only for server-side encryption./ppFor more information about S3 client-side encryption, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingClientSideEncryption.html"Protecting data using client-side encryption./ppFor more information about S3 managed encryption keys, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingServerSideEncryption.html"Using server-side encryption with Amazon S3-managed encryption keys (SSE-S3).

question_content: pA company is running its website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. A developer needs to secure the internet-facing connection with HTTPS. The developer uses AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue an X.509 certificate./ppWhat should the developer do to secure the connection?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the ALB to use the X.509 certificate by using the AWS Management Console.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. ACM can give you the ability to create, store, and renew the public and private SSL/TLS X.509 certificates and keys that protect many AWS websites and applications. You can configure the certificates for use with an ALB./ppFor more information about ACM, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/acm-overview.html"What Is AWS Certificate Manager?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure each EC2 instance to use the same X.509 certificate by using the AWS Management Console.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. ACM can give you the ability to create, store, and renew the public and private SSL/TLS X.509 certificates and keys that protect many AWS websites and applications. However, you cannot configure the certificates for use with EC2 instances directly unless the certificates are part of an AWS Nitro Enclave. This scenario does not use a Nitro Enclave./ppFor more information about Nitro Enclaves, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/enclaves/latest/user/nitro-enclave-refapp.html"Nitro Enclaves application: AWS Certificate Manager for Nitro Enclaves.

answer_choices.choice_content: pExport the root key of the X.509 certificate to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure each EC2 instance to use the same X.509 certificate from the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. ACM can give you the ability to create, store, and renew the public and private SSL/TLS X.509 certificates and keys that protect many AWS websites and applications. However, you cannot export the root certificates from ACM.

answer_choices.choice_content: pExport the root key of the X.509 certificate to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the ALB to use the X.509 certificate from the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. ACM can give you the ability to create, store, and renew the public and private SSL/TLS X.509 certificates and keys that protect many AWS websites and applications. You can configure the certificates for use with an ALB. However, you cannot perform this process by exporting the root certificate because this step is not possible with ACM.

question_content: pAn application stores financial statements in an Amazon S3 bucket. A recent security audit found that the bucket does not comply with company standards. Currently, several IAM policies allow encrypted calls and unencrypted calls to the bucket. The company needs to create a bucket policy that forces all requests to the bucket to use encrypted connections./ppWhich solution will meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd a bucket policy with a condition of "aws:SecureTransport": "true" and an effect of "Allow."
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. If you allow an "aws:SecureTransport": "true" condition, you will allow any attempts to connect to the S3 bucket through HTTPS. However, this condition will not affect any attempts to connect to the S3 bucket through HTTP if other policies already allow the attempts./ppFor more information about how to enforce data encryption in transit with Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security-best-practices.html"Security Best Practices for Amazon S3.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd a bucket policy with a resource of "arn:aws:s3:::https/bucketname" and an effect of "Allow."
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot use the resource section of a bucket policy to enforce encrypted connections to an S3 bucket./ppFor more information about bucket policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-policies.html"Using bucket policies.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd a bucket policy with a condition of "aws:SecureTransport": "false" and an effect of "Deny."
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. If you deny an "aws:SecureTransport": "false" condition, you will not allow any attempts to connect to the S3 bucket through HTTP, even if other policies allow such connections./ppFor more information about how to enforce data encryption in transit with Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/security-best-practices.html"Security Best Practices for Amazon S3.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd a bucket policy with a resource of "arn:aws:s3:::http/bucketname" and an effect of "Deny."
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot use the resource section of the bucket policy to enforce the use of encrypted connections to an S3 bucket./ppFor more information about bucket policies, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-policies.html"Using bucket policies.

question_content: pA developer uses server-side encryption with customer-provided encryption keys (SSE-C) to upload data to Amazon S3. Later, the developer wants to decrypt and download an encrypted object by using the GetObject API call./p	pWhich information must the developer provide to meet this requirement?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe S3 object key and a randomly salted HMAC (Hash Message Authentication Code) value for the encryption key
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon S3 stores a randomly salted HMAC value for the encryption key with the object's metadata. Amazon S3 uses the salted HMAC value to validate future requests. It is not possible to use the HMAC value to derive the value of the encryption key.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe S3 object key and the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The KMS key is used with server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). This developer is using SSE-C, not SSE-KMS.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe S3 object key and the encryption key
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The GetObject API call must specify the customer-provided encryption key that is used to initially encrypt the data./ppFor more information about the GetObject API, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/API/API_GetObject.html"GetObject./ppFor more information about SSE-C, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/ServerSideEncryptionCustomerKeys.html"Using server-side encryption with customer-provided encryption keys (SSE-C).

answer_choices.choice_content: pOnly the S3 object key
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The GetObject API call must specify the customer-provided encryption key that is used to initially encrypt the data.

question_content: pA company has two different applications that must share sensitive data that the company stores in Amazon S3. A Java application uses the AWS Encryption SDK to encrypt an object before the application uploads it to Amazon S3. Later, a Python application written with the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) downloads and decrypts the object by using the S3 encryption client. The decrypt operation produces results that are unreadable, even though both clients have the correct IAM permissions and specify the same Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key./ppWhich action will decrypt the object?

answer_choices.choice_content: pRewrite the decryption client in Java to perform encryption and decryption in the same language.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The Encryption SDK and the S3 encryption client are not compatible because they produce ciphertexts with different data formats./ppFor more information about the Encryption SDK and language-specific SDKs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/introduction.html"What Is the AWS Encryption SDK?

answer_choices.choice_content: pRewrite the Python application to perform decryption by using the Encryption SDK instead of the S3 encryption client.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The Amazon S3 encryption client cannot decrypt data that the Encryption SDK has encrypted. You must use the Encryption SDK for both encryption and decryption operations, or you must use S3 client-side encryption/the S3 encryption client for both encryption and decryption operations./ppFor more information about the AWS Encryption SDK vs language-specific SDKs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/encryption-sdk/latest/developer-guide/introduction.html"What Is the AWS Encryption SDK?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a common IAM role for use by both clients. Ensure that both clients use the same role.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The two clients do not need to use the same IAM roles. IAM roles are not part of encryption or decryption operations./ppFor more information about IAM roles, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles.html"IAM roles.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that the two clients use the same IAM credentials.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The two clients do not need to use the same IAM credentials. IAM credentials are not part of encryption or decryption operations./ppFor more information about AWS credentials, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-security-credentials.html"AWS security credentials.

question_content: pA company's developer is creating an AWS Lambda function that will read data from an Amazon RDS database. The company's security policies require the database credentials to be encrypted at rest by AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys. The database credentials must also be automatically rotated. The Lambda function needs to be able to read the database credentials securely./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Secrets Manager secret for the database credentials encrypted with a KMS key. Modify the Lambda function to retrieve the secret from Secrets Manager. Attach a custom IAM policy to the Lambda function execution role to allow access to secretsmanager:GetSecretValue from the secret's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) and to allow access to kms:Decrypt from the KMS key's ARN.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Secrets Manager can store secrets that AWS KMS encrypts at rest. Secrets Manager also supports the automatic rotation of database credentials. You can use IAM permissions to control access to the secret value of the database credentials./ppFor more information about Secrets Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html"What Is AWS Secrets Manager?a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html" /a/ppFor more information about how to rotate secrets in Secrets Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotating-secrets.html"Rotate AWS Secrets Manager Secrets.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon S3 bucket for the database credentials. Encrypt the database credentials with server-side encryption with KMS keys (SSE-KMS). Modify the Lambda function to retrieve the database credentials from the S3 bucket. Attach a custom IAM policy to the Lambda function execution role to allow access to S3:GetObject from the S3 bucket's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) and to allow access to kms:Decrypt from the KMS key's ARN.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon S3 supports server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS). However, Amazon S3 cannot automatically rotate the database credentials. Additionally, Amazon S3 is not a suitable option for Lambda to query for database credentials./ppFor more information about Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Welcome.html"What Is Amazon S3?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate SecureString parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for the database credentials encrypted with a KMS key. Pass the parameter values by using Lambda environment variables. Attach a custom IAM policy to the Lambda function execution role to allow access to ssm:GetParameter from the parameter's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) and to allow access to kms:Decrypt from the KMS key's ARN.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Parameter Store can store the database credentials as SecureString parameters by using AWS KMS to encrypt the database credentials. However, Parameter Store cannot automatically rotate the database credentials./ppFor more information about Parameter Store features, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html#parameter-store-features"What Are the Features of Parameter Store?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate String parameters in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for the database credentials encrypted with a KMS key. Pass the parameter values by using Lambda environment variables. Attach a custom IAM policy to the Lambda function execution role to allow access to ssm:GetParameter from the parameter's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) and to allow access to kms:Decrypt from the KMS key's ARN.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Parameter Store can store the database credentials as String parameters. However, String parameters would be plain text. You cannot encrypt String parameters with a KMS key. Additionally, Parameter Store cannot automatically rotate the database credentials./ppFor more information about Parameter Store features, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html#parameter-store-features"What Are the Features of Parameter Store?a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html#parameter-store-features" /a

question_content: pA company is storing its application logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The logs must be encrypted at rest by an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. A developer is working on an application that is in violation of this requirement./ppWhat should the developer do to comply with this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pDelete the CloudWatch Logs log group. Create a new log group by using the AWS CLI. Create an asymmetric KMS customer managed key. Associate the key with the new log group.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudWatch Logs supports only symmetric customer managed keys.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDelete the CloudWatch Logs log group. Create a new log group by using the AWS Management Console. Create a symmetric KMS customer managed key. Associate the key with the new log group.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot use the console to encrypt CloudWatch Logs log groups with a customer managed key. You must use the AWS CLI associate-kms-key or the create-log-group API call to encrypt log groups.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the existing CloudWatch Logs log group by using the AWS CLI. Create a symmetric KMS customer managed key. Associate the key with the log group.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. To use a customer managed key, you must encrypt CloudWatch Logs log groups by using the AWS CLI. Additionally, the customer managed key must be a symmetric key./ppFor more information about how to encrypt CloudWatch Logs log groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/encrypt-log-data-kms.html"Encrypt Log Data in CloudWatch Logs Using AWS Key Management Service.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the existing CloudWatch Logs log group by using the AWS Management Console. Create a symmetric KMS customer managed key. Associate the key with the log group.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot use the console to encrypt CloudWatch Logs log groups. You must use the AWS CLI associate-kms-key or the create-log-group API call to encrypt log groups.

question_content: pA company is building a cloud solution to analyze customer demographic data. The data includes personally identifiable information (PII) such as full names, street addresses, and financial records./ppA developer is configuring a source Amazon DynamoDB table with a DynamoDB stream. The developer is writing an AWS Lambda function that will ingest the demographic data from the DynamoDB stream, perform analytics, and write results to a separate DynamoDB table. The application must log important AWS API workflow events for monitoring purposes, but the application must not expose the PII./ppWhich combination of actions should the developer take to log the LARGEST amount of AWS API operational information in the application without exposing the PII? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the DynamoDB stream to record KEYS_ONLY events.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. KEYS_ONLY events record only the partition and sort keys of changed DynamoDB items. /ppFor more information about DynamoDB streams, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_StreamSpecification.html"StreamSpecification.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the DynamoDB stream to record NEW_IMAGE events.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. NEW_IMAGE events contain the entire database item, including PII. A log of this event would expose the PII./ppFor more information about DynamoDB streams, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_StreamSpecification.html"StreamSpecification.

answer_choices.choice_content: pLog the received event. Fetch the items from the source DynamoDB table. Log only the response metadata from the API. Process and record the result in the separate DynamoDB table. Log only the response metadata from the API.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A log that includes KEYS_ONLY events will not expose any PII. This solution is an effective component of workflow event logs. A log of only the API response metadata will not expose customer PII. This solution exposes only the metadata about the specific API request./ppFor more information about the API metadata object, see href="https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/guide/error-handling.html#parsing-error-responses-and-catching-exceptions-from-aws-services"Parsing Error Responses and Catching Exceptions from AWS Services.

answer_choices.choice_content: pLog the received event. Fetch the items from the source DynamoDB table. Log the response from the API. Process and record the result in the separate DynamoDB table. Log the response from the API.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A log of the entire API response from DynamoDB will include all item attributes, including PII. A log of the API response would not be secure because PII is in the table. /ppFor more information about DynamoDB API calls, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_GetItem.html#API_GetItem_ResponseSyntax"Response Syntax.

answer_choices.choice_content: pFetch the items from the source DynamoDB table. Process the data and log workflow events without referring to the PII. Record the result in the separate DynamoDB table.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This solution is a viable way to mask PII that is received from the API call. However, this solution does not meet the requirement to log important AWS API workflow events. It is difficult to monitor API calls that are failing from the Lambda function's logs.

question_content: pA developer is creating an API that provides predictive analysis about stock market trends. The developer wants the API to be publicly accessible but also wants to implement a gating factor so that the requests do not overwhelm the API./ppThe developer decides to require a shared secret to authenticate requests to the API. The developer must implement a solution to rotate the secret every 90 days and to encrypt the secret at rest. The solution also must update AWS Lambda functions in the same environment that call the API so that the Lambda functions will use the rotated secret. The developer will provide the rotated secret to subscribers in a third-party private chatroom./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST development effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString parameter that stores the shared secret value. Update the Lambda functions and API to pull the secret from Parameter Store. Create a Lambda function that generates a new secret string that updates the parameter. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the Lambda function based on a cron schedule every 90 days.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Parameter Store does not provide automatic secret rotation. Additionally, this solution requires you to write custom code, so this solution requires additional development effort. Instead, you can use Secrets Manager to implement automatic key rotation lifecycles. You can configure automatic rotation of secrets and aliases in Secrets Manager, which automates most of the process and involves less development effort./ppFor more information about Parameter Store, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html"AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Secrets Manager to generate a shared secret value. Update the Lambda functions and API to pull the secret from Secrets Manager. Use the SecretsManagerRotationTemplate provided by Secrets Manager to create the Lambda function that generates and stores a new secret. Configure the secret to rotate every 90 days. Select the newly created Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. This solution requires the least amount of development effort. You can manage the rotation schedule in Secrets Manager. You must update the API and Lambda functions with a single API call to pull the secret from Secrets Manager. Secrets Manager is the most suitable solution because it is designed for secrets. Secrets Manager turns on encryption by default, and you cannot turn off the encryption. Secrets Manager can automatically handle secret rotation./ppFor more information about how to set up automatic rotation for Secrets Manager secrets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_turn-on-for-other.html"Set Up Automatic Rotation for AWS Secrets Manager Secrets Using the Console. /ppFor more information about Secrets Manager rotation function templates, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/reference_available-rotation-templates.html#sar-template-generic"AWS Secrets Manager Rotation Function Templates.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon S3 bucket that stores the shared secret value. Configure the S3 bucket to use object versioning. Update the Lambda functions and API to pull the secret from Amazon S3. Create a Lambda function that generates a new secret string that updates the S3 object. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the Lambda function based on a cron schedule every 90 days.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use Amazon S3, turn on encryption, and use an EventBridge rule to invoke a Lambda function on a schedule to rotate secrets. This solution is fully manual. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirement to minimize developmental effort./ppFor more information about Amazon S3 use cases, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/getting-started-next-steps.html#s3-use-cases"Understand Common Use Cases.

answer_choices.choice_content: pWrite code in the API that generates a shared secret value. Store a timestamp as an environment variable that the API can reference to ensure that the secret is rotated every 90 days. Configure the API to update the Lambda function environment variables to use the new secret key each time the key is rotated.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. There is no native functionality to implement secret rotation in this solution. To rotate secrets, you would need to add a service, such as EventBridge, to invoke the Lambda function to rotate on a schedule./ppFor more information about Secrets Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html"What Is AWS Secrets Manager?

question_content: pA development team sets up a project's file directory structure in AWS CodeCommit. The team plans to use AWS CodeBuild and AWS CodeDeploy. The team creates the necessary configuration files for CodeBuild and CodeDeploy. The team wants to name and place these files according to service defaults./ppWhere should the team place the CodeBuild and CodeDeploy files?
