answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The CodeBuild buildspec.yml file and the CodeDeploy appspec.yml file should be in the root of the source directory.

answer_choices.choice_content: pA directory named "deploy" under the root source directory
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The CodeBuild buildspec.yml file and the CodeDeploy appspec.yml file should be in the root of the source directory.

answer_choices.choice_content: pA directory named "scripts" under the root source directory
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The CodeBuild buildspec.yml file and the CodeDeploy appspec.yml file should be in the root of the source directory.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe root of the source directory
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The CodeBuild buildspec.yml file and the CodeDeploy appspec.yml file should be in the root of the source directory./ppFor more information about the CodeBuild buildspec.yaml file, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html#build-spec-ref-name-storage"Buildspec file name and storage location./ppFor more information about the CodeDeploy appspec.yaml file, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/reference-appspec-file-validate.html"Validate your AppSpec File and file location.

question_content: pA developer is preparing a deployment package for a Java implementation of an AWS Lambda function./p	pWhat should the developer include in the deployment package? (Select TWO.)/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pJava runtime environment
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Lambda provides Java runtime, so there is no need to include it in the deployment package./ppFor more information about building Lambda functions with Java, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-java.html" tabindex="-1"Building Lambda functions with Java.

answer_choices.choice_content: pReferences to the event sources
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The event sources are external to Lambda and are used to invoke a Lambda function. As such, event sources are not part of a Lambda deployment package./ppFor more information about event source mapping in Lambda, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-eventsourcemapping.html" tabindex="-1"AWS Lambda event source mappings.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCompiled application code
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. To create a Lambda function, you first create a Lambda function deployment package. This deployment package is a .zip or .jar file consisting of your code and any dependencies. /ppFor more information about Lambda deployment packages, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-package.html%20" tabindex="-1"Lambda deployment packages. /ppFor more information about deploying a Lambda application, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/applications-tutorial.html" tabindex="-1"Creating an application with continuous delivery in the Lambda console.

answer_choices.choice_content: pLambda execution role
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A Lambda execution role is an IAM role that grants the function permission to access AWS services and resources. This role is provided when a Lambda function is created. It is not included in the deployment package. /ppFor more information about Lambda execution roles, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-intro-execution-role.html" tabindex="-1"AWS Lambda execution role.

answer_choices.choice_content: pApplication dependencies
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. To create a Lambda function, you first create a Lambda function deployment package. This package is a .zip or .jar file consisting of your code and any dependencies. /ppFor more information about Lambda deployment packages, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-package.html%20" tabindex="-1"Lambda deployment packages. /ppFor more information about deploying a Lambda application, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/applications-tutorial.html" tabindex="-1"Creating an application with continuous delivery in the Lambda console.

question_content: pA company is developing a new cloud printing platform. The platform design is fully serverless. The platform will use many different AWS Lambda functions to provide functionality. Many of the Lambda functions will need to use a common set of dependencies. The company wants the ability to centrally manage and update the dependencies as needed. The company does not want to update each Lambda function individually./p	pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of code written?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a zip file with the dependencies. Create a Lambda layer that references the zip file in the Lambda console. Add the layer to the configuration of each Lambda function that requires the dependency.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Lambda layers allow developers to share prerequisites such as libraries, custom runtimes, data, or configuration files. Layers also promote code sharing and faster iteration of Lambda code./ppFor more information about how to share dependencies with many Lambda functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-layers.html"Creating and sharing Lambda layers.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a zip file with the dependencies. Upload the zip file to an Amazon S3 bucket. Load the dependency object from Amazon S3 into each Lambda function that requires the dependency.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use Amazon S3 as a repository for files you intend to share. However, if you store the dependencies in a zip file, the Lambda environment would potentially need to retrieve that file at every invocation. This solution would require a significant amount of new code for each Lambda function that requires the dependencies. You can use Lambda layers to avoid the need for the code that is necessary to retrieve the dependencies at each invocation./ppFor more information about Amazon S3, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/Welcome.html"What Is Amazon S3?/ppFor more information about how to share dependencies with many Lambda functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-layers.html"Creating and sharing Lambda layers.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a Docker container image with the dependencies. Publish the image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Configure the Lambda functions that require the dependencies as containers, based on the image in Amazon ECR.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can package and deploy Lambda functions as container images, so you would need to bundle the dependencies with the code in the image. This solution would not meet the requirement to manage the dependencies centrally./ppFor more information about how to use container images with Lambda, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/images-create.html"Creating Lambda container images.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a repository in AWS CodeCommit. Add dependency code to the CodeCommit repository. Use Git commands to access the dependency code in each Lambda function that requires the dependency.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Although CodeCommit is a code repository, dependency storage would require the Lambda function to include code to retrieve the dependencies at every invocation. You can use Lambda layers to avoid the need for the code that is necessary to retrieve the dependencies at each invocation./ppFor more information about CodeCommit, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/welcome.html"What Is AWS CodeCommit?/ppFor more information about how to share dependencies with many Lambda functions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-layers.html"Creating and sharing Lambda layers.

question_content: pA company is developing a global website on Amazon EC2 to track flights. The website will use an Amazon RDS database to store flight position and speed information. A developer needs to ensure that the application can securely connect to the database by using the database credentials. The developer also needs to set up automatic rotation of those credentials./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue an X.509 certificate. Configure the application to use the X.509 certificate to connect to the database. Set up automatic certificate rotation.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. ACM can give you the ability to to create, store, and renew the public and private SSL/TLS X.509 certificates and keys that protect many AWS websites and applications. You cannot use the certificates to authenticate a connection to Amazon RDS./ppFor more information about ACM, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/acm/latest/userguide/acm-overview.html"What Is AWS Certificate Manager?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to store the database credentials. Configure the application to use the Parameter Store to retrieve the database credentials. Set up automatic secret rotation.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Parameter Store provides secure, hierarchical storage for configuration data management and secrets management. Parameter Store can store data, including passwords, database strings, Amazon Machine Image (AMI) IDs, and license codes as parameter values. However, Parameter Store does not support automatic rotation of credentials./ppFor more information about Parameter Store, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/sysman-paramstore-su-create.html"Creating Systems Manager parameters.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to create a new encryption key. Encrypt the RDS database credentials with the KMS key. Allow EC2 instances to use the key. Set up KMS encryption key rotation.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS KMS is a managed service that can give you the ability to create and control the encryption keys that are used to encrypt data on AWS. Although it is possible to encrypt credentials, AWS KMS has no way to securely store or distribute credentials to applications./ppFor more information about AWS KMS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/overview.html"AWS Key Management Service.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Secrets Manager to store the database credentials. Configure the application to use Secrets Manager to retrieve the database credentials. Set up automatic secret rotation.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Secrets Manager can store and distribute credentials programmatically from a central and secure datastore. Secrets Manager can also automatically rotate the secrets according to a specified schedule./ppFor more information about Secrets Manager, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/intro.html"What Is AWS Secrets Manager?

question_content: pA developer created configuration specifications for an AWS Elastic Beanstalk application in a file named healthcheckurl.yaml in the .ebextensions/ directory of their application source bundle. The file contains the following:/ppspan style="font-family: Courier New"option_settings:/span/ppspan style="font-family: Courier New"  - namespace: aws:elasticbeanstalk:application/span/ppspan style="font-family: Courier New"    option_name: Application Healthcheck URL/span/ppspan style="font-family: Courier New"    value: /health_check/span/ppAfter the application launches, the health check is not being run on the correct path, even though it is valid./ppWhat can be done to correct this configuration file?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConvert the file to JSON format.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A solution that converts the file to JSON does not solve the issue because configuration files can be either YAML-formatted or JSON-formatted documents./ppFor more information about .ebextensions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/ebextensions.html"Advanced Environment Customization with Configuration Files (.ebextensions).

answer_choices.choice_content: pRename the file to a .config extension.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Configuration files in the .ebextensions folder should be saved with the .config extension. After the change is deployed, the application performs health checks by using the /health_check URL./ppFor more information about .ebextensions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/ebextensions.html"Advanced Environment Customization with Configuration Files (.ebextensions).

answer_choices.choice_content: pChange the configuration section from span style="font-family: Courier New"option_settings/span to span style="font-family: Courier New"resources/span.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The resources section adds or customizes resources that are part of your environment. However, the resources section does not change application configuration./ppFor more information about custom resources in Elastic Beanstalk, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/environment-resources.html"Adding and Customizing Elastic Beanstalk Environment Resources. /ppFor more information about .ebextensions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/ebextensions.html"Advanced Environment Customization with Configuration Files (.ebextensions).

answer_choices.choice_content: pChange the namespace of the option settings to a custom namespace.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. During application deployment, unknown namespaces are ignored. Custom options can collect user-specified settings that use the resources section./ppFor more information about custom options, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/configuration-options-custom.html"Custom Options. /ppFor more information about option settings, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/ebextensions-optionsettings.html"Option Settings.

question_content: pA developer has a new serverless application that is composed of three AWS Lambda functions and an Amazon DynamoDB table. The developer needs to package and deploy all the components together as a single unit. The developer also must run unit tests for the package locally on a desktop./ppWhich automation tool can the developer use to meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pAWS Elastic Beanstalk deployment
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use Elastic Beanstalk to quickly deploy applications and manage applications in the AWS Cloud. You do not need to learn about the infrastructure that runs the applications that you deploy and manage. However, you cannot deploy Lambda functions and a DynamoDB table as a single unit by using Elastic Beanstalk./ppFor more information about Elastic Beanstalk, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/Welcome.html"What Is AWS Elastic Beanstalk?a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/Welcome.html" /a

answer_choices.choice_content: pAWS CloudFormation nested stack
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A nested stack is a stack that you can create as part of another stack. A CloudFormation nested stack can deploy Lambda functions. However, a nested stack does not run unit tests locally. /ppFor more information about CloudFormation nested stacks, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-nested-stacks.html"Working with Nested Stacks.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAWS CodeDeploy stage
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A CodeDeploy deployment can deploy Lambda functions. However, you cannot deploy Lambda functions and a DynamoDB table as a single unit by using CodeDeploy./ppFor more information about deployments on a Lambda compute platform, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployment-steps-lambda.html"Deployments on an AWS Lambda Compute Platform.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) template
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AWS SAM is an open-source framework for building serverless applications. AWS SAM is the only option that gives you the ability to run tests locally and deploy a serverless Lambda application./ppFor more information about how to deploy serverless Lambda applications, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/serverless-application-model/latest/developerguide/serverless-deploying.html"Deploying Serverless Applications.

question_content: pAn education company is developing an integration testing strategy for releases of a new learning management platform. The platform is fully serverless and consists of two parts. The frontend includes static assets stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The backend is an Amazon API Gateway REST API integrated with an AWS Lambda function. The data is stored in an Amazon DynamoDB table. /ppFor the integration tests, the company is creating a separate test environment that includes a copy of each architectural component. The company already has created the backend components for the new test environment. A developer needs to create the frontend components for the new test environment./ppWhich combination of steps should the developer take to meet this requirement? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new Lambda function version. For the new function version, create environment variables that point to the new environment's S3 bucket and DynamoDB table. Create a new function alias that points to the new function version.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Lambda function versions give you the ability to specify different function code, dependencies, and settings such as environment variables. This solution gives you the ability to create a separate set of frontend components for the test environment./ppFor more information about Lambda function versions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-versions.html"Lambda Function Versions.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new Lambda function alias. For the new function alias, create environment variables that point to the new environment's S3 bucket and DynamoDB table. Create a new function version that points to the new function alias.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A Lambda alias does not give you the ability to modify the function configuration. An alias is a reference to a Lambda function version or a weighted route between multiple versions. You cannot create environment variables for the function alias. /ppFor more information about Lambda function aliases, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-aliases.html"Lambda Function Aliases.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new stage for the API. Configure the stage integration to point to the Lambda function name and alias for the new environment.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. API stage configurations do not give you the ability to specify a different integration. API deployment snapshots define integrations. You must specify different integration endpoints as a stage variable. /ppFor more information about how to set up Lambda integrations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-lambda-integrations.html"Set Up Lambda Integrations in API Gateway.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new stage for the API. Create a stage variable with a value of the Lambda function Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the new environment.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use a stage variable instead of a Lambda function name, version, or alias. API Gateway will dynamically translate the function name, version, and alias to the full ARN. You cannot use a stage variable with a value of the Lambda function ARN. /ppFor more information about how to set stage variables, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-set-stage-variables-aws-console.html"Setting Stage Variables Using the Amazon API Gateway Console.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new stage for the API. Create a stage variable with values of the Lambda function name and alias for the new environment.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use API Gateway stage variables to specify Lambda function versions or aliases to use in the stage. API Gateway will dynamically translate the stage variables into the full ARN. This solution gives you the ability to create a separate set of frontend components for the test environment./ppFor more information about how to set stage variables, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-set-stage-variables-aws-console.html"Setting Stage Variables Using the Amazon API Gateway Console.

question_content: pA company deploys Amazon API Gateway backed by several AWS Lambda functions. The company uses two stages, dev and prod, to separate production from ongoing development. The company defines dev and prod aliases for each Lambda function. The company must ensure the prod stage references only production-ready Lambda functions./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pFor each API Gateway stage, modify each integration request's Lambda function name to include a suffix of :dev or :prod as appropriate.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. API Gateway stages do not provide a way to configure individual integration requests./ppFor more information about API Gateway stages, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-deploy-api.html"Deploying a REST API in Amazon API Gateway.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDefine an API Gateway stage variable named ENV for each stage. Set the variable to dev or prod as appropriate. Modify each integration request's Lambda function name to include a suffix of :${stageVariables.ENV}.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. API Gateway stages define stage variables. The variables can have different values for different stages. Integration requests define API Gateway resource/method integrations, including Lambda functions. Lambda function references can include dynamic references to stage variables./ppFor more information about API Gateway stage variables, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/stage-variables.html"Setting up stage variables for a REST API deployment.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDefine two Lambda destinations for each Lambda function named dev and prod, respectively. For each API Gateway stage, modify each integration request's Lambda function name to include a suffix of :dev or :prod as appropriate.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use Lambda destinations to record asynchronous function results and send those results to another resource. API Gateway does not use the Lambda destinations to determine which Lambda function version or alias to invoke. Also, API Gateway stages do not provide a way to configure individual integration requests./ppFor more information about how to use Lambda destinations for asynchronous invocations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async.html#invocation-async-destinations"Configuring destinations for asynchronous invocation.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDefine a prod resource group that contains all prod Lambda aliases. Define another resource group for dev. For each API Gateway stage, modify each integration request's Lambda function name to include a suffix of :dev or :prod as appropriate.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS resource groups are a general way to define and manage a group of AWS resources as a set. API Gateway does not use AWS resource groups to determine which Lambda function version or alias to invoke. Also, API Gateway stages do not provide a way to configure individual integration requests./ppFor more information about resource groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ARG/latest/userguide/resource-groups.html"What are resource groups?

question_content: pA developer is deploying an AWS Lambda function by using an AWS CloudFormation template that uses an AWS::Lambda::Function resource. Events that the Lambda function cannot successfully process must be stored in a durable location for processing later./ppHow should the developer configure the Lambda function in the CloudFormation template to meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd a TracingConfig property to the AWS::Lambda::Function resource with tracing mode set to Active to write unsuccessful events to AWS X-Ray.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. X-Ray is a service that collects data about requests that your application serves. However, X-Ray does not capture unsuccessful events./ppFor more information about X-Ray, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/aws-xray.html"What Is AWS X-Ray?a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/aws-xray.html" /a

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS::SNS::Topic resource in the template with an email-json subscription. Add a DeadLetterConfig property to the AWS::Lambda::Function resource. In the DeadLetterConfig property, reference the topic's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the TargetArn property.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A solution that sends unsuccessful events to an AWS::SNS::Topic with an email-json subscription will deliver events to an email address. Email notification is not a durable storage solution./ppFor more information about Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) email notifications, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-email-notifications.html"Email Notifications.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd an EphemeralStorage property to the AWS::Lambda::Function resource. Configure the Lambda function to write unsuccessful events to the ephemeral storage.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The Lambda ephemeral storage is a temporary directory not intended for durable storage./ppFor more information about the ephemeral storage data type, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/API_EphemeralStorage.html"EphemeralStorage. /ppFor more information about how to configure ephemeral storage, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-function-common.html#configuration-ephemeral-storage"Configuring Ephemeral Storage (Console).

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS::SQS::Queue resource in the template. Add a DeadLetterConfig property to the AWS::Lambda::Function resource. In the DeadLetterConfig property, reference the queue's Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the TargetArn property.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) dead-letter queue offers message durability and can store unsuccessful Lambda events for processing later. /ppFor more information about how to use dead-letter queues with Lambda, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async.html#invocation-dlq"Dead-Letter Queues. /ppFor more information about how to use CloudFormation to configure Lambda dead-letter queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/aws-properties-lambda-function-deadletterconfig.html"AWS::Lambda::Function DeadLetterConfig.

question_content: pA customer wants to deploy its source code on an AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment. The customer needs to perform deployment with minimal outage and should use only existing instances./ppWhich deployment policy would satisfy these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pRolling
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Rolling deployment splits the instances into batches and deploys one batch at a time. Rolling deployment does not initiate a new service. Rolling deployment continues sending requests. However, you can experience an outage in the service./ppFor more information about how to deploy applications to Elastic Beanstalk environments, see href="http://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.deploy-existing-version.html"Deploying Applications to Elastic Beanstalk Environments.

answer_choices.choice_content: pAll at once
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The all-at-once deployment method performs in-place deployment on all instances. All-at-once deployment is acceptable if you can accept a short loss of service, such as in the development or QA environment. In this scenario, the customer requires minimal outage time, so this solution is not the best option.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRolling with an additional batch
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The rolling deployment with additional batch option creates additional instances that do not satisfy the requirements to use only existing instances.

answer_choices.choice_content: pImmutable
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The immutable deployment option creates a new set of instances that do not satisfy the requirement to use only existing instances.

question_content: pThe release process workflow of an application requires a manual approval before the code is deployed into the production environment. A developer needs to achieve this using AWS CodePipeline./ppHow should a developer meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse multiple pipelines to allow approval.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A pipeline is composed of multiple stages and actions. Multiple pipelines do not mean that manual approval is automatically added as required in the question./ppFor more information about pipelines, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/pipelines.html"Working with Pipelines in CodePipeline.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an approval action in a stage.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Valid CodePipeline action types are source, build,  test, deploy, approval, and invoke. An approval action is the most appropriate way to accomplish the requirements./ppFor more information about actions in CodePipeline, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/actions.html"Working with Actions in CodePipeline. /ppFor more information about approval actions in CodePipeline, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/approvals.html"Manage Approval Actions in CodePipeline.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDisable the stage transition to allow manual approval.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Transitions are links between pipeline stages. If you deactivate the stage transition, manual approvals are not facilitated./ppFor more information about stage transitions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/transitions.html"Working with Stage Transitions in CodePipeline.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDisable a stage just prior to the deployment stage.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can stop a stage's inbound transition to prevent  executions from entering that stage. You can then start the transition to allow  executions to continue. However, this does not give the manual approval that is required in the question./ppFor more information about CodePipeline concepts, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/concepts.html#concepts-executions"Pipeline Executions.

question_content: pA development team runs an extensive set of automated tests by using an AWS CodeBuild action in an AWS CodePipeline test stage. The tests take 30 minutes to run for each build. The team wants to reduce the time necessary to run the tests by conducting multiple tests in parallel. To accomplish this goal, the team breaks the test into multiple independent segments./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure multiple parallel CodePipeline stages to run each test segment in a CodeBuild action.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodePipeline stages run sequentially. Only actions within the same CodePipeline stage can run in parallel./ppFor more information about CodePipeline stages, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/pipelines-create.html" tabindex="-1"Create a pipeline in CodePipeline.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure multiple parallel CodeBuild actions to run each segment within the CodePipeline test stage.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CodeBuild can run test actions. A single CodePipeline stage can run many CodeBuild actions in parallel./ppFor more information about CodePipeline actions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/actions.html" tabindex="-1"Working with actions in CodePipeline.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure multiple sequential CodeBuild actions to run each segment within the CodePipeline test stage.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeBuild can run test actions. A single CodePipeline stage can run many CodeBuild actions in sequence. However, this process would not reduce the testing time because the tests would still run sequentially, not in parallel./ppFor more information about CodePipeline actions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/actions.html" tabindex="-1"Working with actions in CodePipeline.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the CodeBuild build environment to use the BUILD_GENERAL1_2XLARGE compute type. Run each test in sequence within the CodePipeline test stage.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeBuild supports a variety of build environments that have different levels of resources. However, this architecture would not run the tests in parallel./ppFor more information about CodeBuild environments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-env-ref-compute-types.html" tabindex="-1"Build environment compute types.

question_content: pA development team uses AWS CodeBuild to build an application. The developers observe that downloads of large dependency files consume most of the time on each build. The downloaded dependency files are stored in a /.m2 folder. The builds are run frequently./p	pWhich set of actions would MOST improve build performance?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the CodeBuild project to implement Amazon S3 caching. Modify the buildspec's cache settings to include a path to the /.m2 folder.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A cache can store reusable pieces of your build environment and use these pieces across multiple builds. S3 caching stores the cache in an S3 bucket that is available across multiple build hosts. This is not the ideal option for large build artifacts because the artifacts can take a long time to transfer over your network, which can affect build performance. /ppFor more information about caching in CodeBuild, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-caching.html"Build caching in AWS CodeBuild.

answer_choices.choice_content: pModify the CodeBuild project to implement local caching. Modify the buildspec's cache settings to include a path to the /.m2 folder.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A cache can store reusable pieces of your build environment and use them across multiple builds. Local caching stores a cache on a build host. When dependency files are large or builds are frequent, local caching helps to avoid large, repetitive downloads that can slow builds./ppFor more information about caching in CodeBuild, see span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-caching.html"Build caching in AWS CodeBuild.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a shared CodeBuild project. Call the PutResourcePolicy API to include a path to the /.m2 folder as a shared resource.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A shared CodeBuild project is accessible to other AWS accounts and users. The PutResourcePolicy API allows an owner to designate the principals with whom the project is shared. A shared CodeBuild project does not cache or pre-download any resources. For this reason, it will not improve the build performance./ppFor more information about shared CodeBuild projects, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/project-sharing.html"Working with shared projects.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS CodeArtifact repository as an upstream repository. Modify the build settings with the repository URI and authorization token.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeArtifact is a fully managed artifact repository service compatible with package managers. It is mainly used by companies to address security concerns by storing approved artifacts within an AWS account. A CodeArtifact repository would have a negligible effect on performance when compared to caching./ppFor more information about CodeArtifact, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/welcome.html"What is AWS CodeArtifact?

question_content: pA development team uses AWS CodeBuild for build and test activities in a PHP application. The build process requires the team to download and install three PHP packages from the internet. The install section of the buildspec.yml file includes commands to download and install these three packages. The team wants to reduce build time./p	pWhich solution will reduce build time the MOST?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pDownload the package files from the internet. Upload the package files into an Amazon S3 bucket. Change the buildspec's install section to use the S3 bucket as the download location.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You might reduce the download time slightly by copying the required packages to an S3 bucket. Download time depends on the original location of the packages and the AWS Region. However, this solution would save less time than a solution that prepares a custom image with the packages pre-installed./ppFor more information about CodeBuild custom images, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/sample-docker-custom-image.html" tabindex="-1"Docker in custom image sample for CodeBuild.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDefine a VPC endpoint for CodeBuild. Install the package files on an Amazon EC2 instance in the VPC. Change the buildspec's install section to use the EC2 instance as the download location.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A VPC-enabled build project can access resources within a VPC. This kind of build project has several use cases, including access to internally hosted package managers. You would likely reduce the download time by downloading the required packages from an EC2 instance. However, a custom build image would eliminate the download and installation time./ppFor more information about how to use CodeBuild with a VPC, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/vpc-support.html" tabindex="-1"Use AWS CodeBuild with Amazon Virtual Private Cloud.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a custom CodeBuild image with the package files already downloaded and installed. Alter the CodeBuild project to use the custom image. Remove the install commands from the buildspec.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A custom CodeBuild image is a Docker image that you create with everything you need to build and test a project. When a developer builds the application, CodeBuild will retrieve the Docker image from the container registry that the project configuration specifies. CodeBuild will use the environment to compile source code, run tests, and package an application. There is no need to download the packages from anywhere upon each build. This solution greatly reduces the build time./ppFor more information about CodeBuild custom images, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/sample-docker-custom-image.html" tabindex="-1"Docker in custom image sample for CodeBuild.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRun the build on Jenkins by using the Jenkins plugin for CodeBuild. Pre-install the packages on the Jenkins server once. Remove the install commands from the buildspec.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The Jenkins plugin for CodeBuild integrates CodeBuild with Jenkins build jobs. This integration process causes Jenkins to send build jobs to CodeBuild instead of to Jenkins build nodes. You would not reduce the build time in CodeBuild by pre-installing the required packages on Jenkins./ppFor more information about the Jenkins plugin for CodeBuild, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/jenkins-plugin.html" tabindex="-1"Use AWS CodeBuild with Jenkins.

question_content: pA developer deploys an ecommerce application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. The EC2 instances are based on an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that uses an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) root volume. After deployment, the developer notices that a third of the instances seem to be idle. These instances are not receiving requests from the load balancer. The developer verifies that all the instances are  registered with the load balancer. The developer must implement a solution to allow the EC2 instances to receive requests from the load balancer./ppWhich action will meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pReregister the failed instances with the ALB.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The most likely cause is an incorrectly configured ALB Availability Zone because the instances are registered. Reregistering the instances with the load balancer would not resolve the issue./ppFor more information about how to register instances, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/target-group-register-targets.html"Register targets with your target group.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable all Availability Zones for the ALB.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The most likely cause is an incorrectly configured ALB Availability Zone because the instances are registered. You can enable and disable Availability Zones at any time. After you enable an Availability Zone, the load balancer starts routing requests to the registered targets in that Availability Zone. This process should resolve the issue./ppFor more information about ALB Availability Zones, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-subnets.html"Availability Zones for your Application Load Balancer.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the instance refresh feature to redeploy the EC2 Auto Scaling group.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The most likely cause is an incorrectly configured ALB Availability Zone because the instances are registered. If you use instance refresh, you will replace the instances. However, the instances would still be in Availability Zones that is not configured properly./ppFor more information about instance refresh, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/asg-instance-refresh.html"Replace Auto Scaling instances based on an instance refresh.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRestart the EC2 instances that are not receiving traffic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The most likely cause is an incorrectly configured ALB Availability Zone because the instances are registered. If you stop and start the instances that are not receiving traffic from the load balancer, you will migrate the instances to a new host. However, because the instances have a root EBS volume, the host would have to remain in the same Availability Zone. This process would not resolve the issue./ppFor more information about how to stop and start EC2 instances, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Stop_Start.html"Stop and start your instance.

question_content: pA developer is building an application using an Amazon API Gateway REST API backed by an AWS Lambda function that interacts with an Amazon DynamoDB table. During testing, the developer observes high latency when making requests to the API./ppHow can the developer evaluate the end-to-end latency and identify performance bottlenecks?

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable AWS CloudTrail logging and use the logs to map each latency and bottleneck.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudTrail can provide records of actions taken  in API Gateway by a user, a role, or an AWS service. CloudTrail captures all REST API calls for API Gateway  service APIs as events. A developer can use CloudTrail logs to troubleshoot API creation, deployment, and updates. However, the logs do not help to identify the bottleneck and cause of latency./ppFor more information about how to log calls to API Gateway APIs with CloudTrail, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/cloudtrail.html"Logging Calls to Amazon API Gateway APIs with AWS CloudTrail.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable and configure AWS X-Ray tracing on API Gateway and the Lambda function. Use X-Ray to trace and analyze user requests.
answer_choices.solution_content: p  Correct. X-Ray gives you the ability to trace latency issues with your API Gateway APIs.  X-Ray provides an end-to-end view of requests as they travel through your application. X-Ray can be used to trace and analyze user requests. These collected traces give you the ability to evaluate the end-to-end latency and identify performance bottlenecks./ppa target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-xray.html"For more information about how to use X-Ray to identify bottlenecks, see span style="text-decoration: underline;"Tracing User Requests to REST APIs Using X-Ray/span/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable Amazon CloudWatch Logs for the Lambda function. Enable execution logs for API Gateway to view and analyze user request logs.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can integrate CloudWatch Logs with API Gateway to debug issues related to requests or client access to your API. CloudWatch Logs integrated with the Lambda function gives you the ability to troubleshoot failures in a function. Because elevated latency does not necessarily correspond to problems with the API request execution or failures in the function, this option is incorrect./ppFor more information about API Gateway logging with CloudWatch, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/set-up-logging.html"Setting Up CloudWatch Logging for a REST API in API Gateway.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable VPC Flow Logs to capture and analyze network traffic within the VPC.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. VPC Flow Logs can help troubleshoot specific traffic flow issues for an instance. However, VPC Flow Logs do not help identify the cause of latency or find performance bottlenecks. Additionally, there is no mention of a VPC within the described architecture. VPC Flow Logs require a VPC./ppFor more information about VPC Flow Logs, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/flow-logs.html"Logging IP Traffic Using VPC Flow Logs.

question_content: pA company hosts a web application that writes to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Application users frequently observe and report errors. The development team examines Amazon CloudWatch logs and frequently sees the following error:  /ppspan style="font-family: Courier New"400 Bad Request ProvisionedThroughputExceededException/span/p  pWhat is the cause of this error?

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe application does not have the required permissions for the DynamoDB table.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A ProvisionedThroughputExceededException error indicates that the maximum allowed provisioned throughput for a table, or for one or more global secondary indexes, has been exceeded. A permissions error would return a different error code./ppFor more information about DynamoDB throughput, see ua target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Programming.Errors.html"Error handling with DynamoDB/a/u.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe item that the application is placing on the table exceeds the item size limit.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An attempt to call the PutItem operation that exceeds the maximum item size limit would result in a ValidationException error, not a ProvisionedThroughputExceededException error./ppFor more information about DynamoDB errors, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Programming.Errors.html#Programming.Errors.MessagesAndCodes"Error messages and codes.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe development team has not allocated enough space for the table and its indexes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. There is no practical limit on a table's size. Tables are not constrained by the number of items or the number of bytes./ppFor more information about DynamoDB quotas, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Limits.html#limits-tables"Table size.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe development team has not allocated enough write capacity units (WCU) for the table and its indexes.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. A ProvisionedThroughputExceededException error indicates that the maximum allowed provisioned throughput for a table, or for one or more global secondary indexes, has been exceeded./ppFor more information about DynamoDB throughput, see ua target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Programming.Errors.html"Error handling with DynamoDB/a/u.

question_content: pAn AWS Lambda function accesses two Amazon DynamoDB tables. A developer wants to improve the performance of the Lambda function by identifying bottlenecks in the function./ppHow can the developer inspect the timing of the DynamoDB API calls?

answer_choices.choice_content: pAdd DynamoDB as an event source to the Lambda function. View the performance with Amazon CloudWatch metrics.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The DynamoDB tables are accessed by the Lambda function. Because DynamoDB does not invoke the Lambda function, a DynamoDB event source is not needed. Additionally, CloudWatch metrics cannot inspect API calls./ppFor more information about DynamoDB as a Lambda event source, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-ddb.html"Using AWS Lambda with Amazon DynamoDB. /ppFor more information about CloudWatch metrics, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/working_with_metrics.html"Using Amazon CloudWatch Metrics.

answer_choices.choice_content: pPlace an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the two DynamoDB tables. Inspect the ALB logs.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can integrate ALB with services, such as Amazon EC2 instances and microservices. However, you cannot integrate ALB with DynamoDB./ppFor more information about ALB targets, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-target-groups.html#target-type"Target Type.

answer_choices.choice_content: pLimit Lambda to no more than five concurrent invocations. Monitor from the Lambda console.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can monitor the number of current invocations in the Lambda console. A solution that monitors or limits the number of concurrent invocations does not decrease the latency of DynamoDB./ppFor more information about Lambda concurrency, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-concurrency.html"Managing Lambda Reserved Concurrency.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable AWS X-Ray tracing for the function. View the traces from the X-Ray service.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use X-Ray to trace the DynamoDB API call from a Lambda function. This solution helps identify performance bottlenecks and facilitate troubleshooting./ppFor more information about X-Ray, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/aws-xray.html"What Is AWS X-Ray?a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/aws-xray.html" /a/ppFor more information about Lambda with X-Ray, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-xray.html"Using AWS Lambda with AWS X-Ray.

question_content: pA development team uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy software changes to Amazon EC2 instances. The deployments begin to fail. The team traces the problem to a specific EC2 instance. The CodeDeploy agent's log file contains the following error message:/p	pspan style="font-family: Courier New"InvalidSignatureException – Signature expired: [time] is now earlier than [time]/span/p	pWhat is the underlying cause of this issue?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe development team signed the CodeDeploy revision after the team created the deployment.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeDeploy does not expect or check signatures on revisions. You can create a deployment only after you create a revision.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe development team signed the CodeDeploy revision with a key that was not valid.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeDeploy does not expect or check signatures on revisions.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe deployment did not finish within the specified time frame.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CodeDeploy deployments do not have a way to specify the maximum acceptable duration of a deployment.

answer_choices.choice_content: pThe date setting or the time setting on the EC2 instance is not correct.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. CodeDeploy requires accurate time references to perform its operations. If the date and time on the instance are not set correctly, the date and time might not match the signature timestamp of the deployment request, which CodeDeploy rejects./ppFor more information about how to troubleshoot CodeDeploy deployments, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/troubleshooting-ec2-instances.html"Troubleshoot instance issues.

question_content: pA company is migrating its application to AWS. A developer must send logs from both on-premises servers and Amazon EC2 instances to AWS for durable storage and visualization./ppWhich solution would meet this requirement with the LEAST developer effort?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Redshift cluster. Rewrite the application to insert log entries into Redshift tables. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data in Redshift tables.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. QuickSight provides the ability to explore and interpret information in an interactive visual environment, including data in Redshift tables. Redshift is a fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse service in the cloud. However, Redshift is optimized to load bulk data, not individual log entries. Significant developer effort would be necessary to rewrite the application to send logs entries to Redshift./ppFor more information about Redshift, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/welcome.html"What Is Amazon Redshift?/ppFor more information about QuickSight, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/welcome.html"What Is Amazon QuickSight?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure Amazon QuickSight with Super-fast, Parallel, In-memory Calculation Engine (SPICE) storage. Rewrite the application to insert log data directly into SPICE. Use QuickSight to visualize the SPICE data.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. QuickSight provides the ability to explore and interpret information in an interactive visual environment. When you import data into a dataset rather than use a direct SQL query, the data becomes SPICE data because of how it is stored. SPICE can rapidly perform advanced calculations and serve data. However, you would need to import each file on every on-premises server and EC2 instance separately. This solution would require significant developer effort to set up. This solution would also require continued effort every time the company creates a new log file./ppFor more information about QuickSight, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/welcome.html"What Is Amazon QuickSight?/ppFor more information about SPICE, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/spice.html"Importing data into SPICE.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon S3 bucket. Rewrite the application to upload log data to Amazon S3. Visualize the log data with Amazon Athena.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Athena is an interactive query service that gives you the ability to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 by using standard SQL. Athena is not designed for visualization. Significant developer effort would be necessary to rewrite the application to send logs entries to Amazon S3./ppFor more information about Athena, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/what-is.html"What Is Amazon Athena/a?/span

answer_choices.choice_content: pDeploy the Amazon CloudWatch agent to both the on-premises servers and the EC2 instances. Visualize the logs through the CloudWatch console.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use the CloudWatch agent to collect logs from EC2 instances and on-premises servers. You can use the CloudWatch console to view CloudWatch logs and graph metrics that are created by using metric filters./ppFor more information about the CloudWatch agent, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Install-CloudWatch-Agent.html"Collecting metrics and logs from Amazon EC2 instances and on-premises servers with the CloudWatch agent./ppFor more information about metrics filters, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/MonitoringLogData.html"Creating metrics from log events using filters./ppFor more information about how to graph metrics, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/graph_metrics.html"Graphing metrics.

question_content: pA company deployed an application as a set of microservices that run on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The performance of the microservices has started to degrade for a specific set of user requests. The company needs to gain deeper insight into the request behavior that is associated with the performance degradation./ppWhich process will meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a Docker image that runs the AWS X-Ray daemon. Run the image alongside the microservices in Amazon ECS. Use the X-Ray console to view requests to the microservices.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. X-Ray is a distributed tracing service that identifies issues and opportunities for optimization in an application where a user request is made across services. X-Ray requires a container to collect tracing data from Amazon ECS./ppFor more information about X-Ray on Amazon ECS, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-daemon-ecs.html"Running the X-Ray daemon on Amazon ECS.

answer_choices.choice_content: pPerform distributed tracing based on the ALB's built-in traffic request metrics.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The ALB automatically distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets, including EC2 instances, containers, and IP addresses. The ALB reports metrics about the requests that flow through the load balancer. However, the ALB does not have the distributed tracing capability that is necessary meet the company's requirement./ppFor more information about metrics that ALBs collect, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-cloudwatch-metrics.html"CloudWatch metrics for your Application Load Balancer.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon CloudWatch to collect metrics and logs from Amazon ECS. Perform distributed tracing based on the ECS metrics and logs.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use CloudWatch to collect and track metrics and logs. However, CloudWatch does not have the distributed tracing capability that is necessary to meet the company's requirement./ppFor more information about CloudWatch, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/WhatIsCloudWatch.html"What is Amazon CloudWatch?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EventBridge rule to capture the ECS metrics and logs. Use the EventBridge console to view the requests to the microservices.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. EventBridge is a serverless event bus service that you can use to connect applications by using data from a variety of sources. EventBridge does not have the distributed tracing capability that is necessary to meet the company's requirement./ppFor more information about EventBridge, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-what-is.html"What Is Amazon EventBridge?

question_content: pA development team uses an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with a subscription to an HTTPS endpoint. A change to the HTTPS endpoint caused the subscription to be misconfigured. It took the development team several days to discover and correct the misconfiguration. Critical messages were lost before the team corrected the subscription. To prevent future message loss, the team must store messages whenever delivery fails./p	pWhich solution will meet this requirement?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pDefine an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as the dead-letter queue for the HTTPS subscription.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An SQS queue can be established as a dead-letter queue associated with an SNS subscription. Any delivery failures are stored on this queue./ppFor more information about dead-letter queues, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-dead-letter-queues.html"Amazon SNS dead-letter queues (DLQs).

answer_choices.choice_content: pDefine a delivery policy to retry delivery every 2 minutes until the HTTPS endpoint is available.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An SNS topic subscription can define a delivery policy to control retry behavior in cases where a delivery fails. A two-minute retry policy would exhaust the maximum number of retry attempts after just a few hours, which would make this solution inadequate for a multi-day outage./ppFor more information about SNS delivery policies, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-message-delivery-retries.html#creating-delivery-policy"Creating an HTTP/S delivery policy.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a failure destination for the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. A failure destination is an option for AWS Lambda functions, not SNS topics. This is not a possible solution./ppFor more information about SNS subscribers, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-create-subscribe-endpoint-to-topic.html"Subscribing to an Amazon SNS topic./ppFor more information about AWS Lambda destinations, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/invocation-async.html#invocation-async-destinations"Configuring destinations for asynchronous invocation.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an Amazon S3 bucket as an additional subscription to the SNS topic.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An S3 bucket cannot subscribe to an SNS topic./ppFor more information about SNS subscribers, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-create-subscribe-endpoint-to-topic.html"Subscribing to an Amazon SNS topic.

question_content: pA company is developing a microservice that will manage customer account data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Insert, update, and delete requests will be rare. Read traffic will be heavy. The company must have the ability to access customer data quickly by using a customer ID. The microservice can tolerate stale data./ppWhich solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST possible read capacity units (RCUs)?

answer_choices.choice_content: pRead the table by using eventually consistent reads.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. DynamoDB provides predictable read performance when you provide a partition key. Eventually consistent reads consume the fewest RCUs. Eventually consistent reads are safe to use because the microservice can tolerate stale data./ppFor more information about DynamoDB read consistency, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/HowItWorks.ReadConsistency.html"Read consistency.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRead the table by using strongly consistent reads.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Strongly consistent reads consume more RCUs than eventually consistent reads. Strongly consistent reads are unnecessary in this case because the company requires tolerance for stale data.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRead the table by using transactional reads.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Transactional reads are necessary only to allow a single API call to predictably retrieve multiple items, potentially from multiple tables. Transactional reads consume more RCUs than eventually consistent reads./ppFor more information about DynamoDB transactions, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/transactions.html"Managing complex workflows with DynamoDB transactions.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRead the table by using strongly consistent PartiQL queries.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. DynamoDB PartiQL queries perform select, insert, update, and delete operations based on an SQL-compatible query language. PartiQL queries provide the same eventual/strong read consistency behavior as the other DynamoDB data plane operations. Strongly consistent reads consume more RCUs than eventually consistent reads. Strongly consistent reads are unnecessary in this case because the company requires tolerance for stale data./ppFor more information about PartiQL with DynamoDB, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/ql-reference.html"PartiQL - a SQL-compatible query language for Amazon DynamoDB.

question_content: pA developer has launched an application that calls an API by way of Amazon API Gateway. It offers information that changes several times a day, but is not updated in real time. The application has become so popular that the API endpoint is overloaded and that traffic to the endpoint must be reduced./ppWhat can the developer do to address the performance issues?

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable API caching in API Gateway.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. API caching in API Gateway improves performance by reducing the number of requests that are sent to your endpoint service./ppFor more information about caching in API Gateway, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-caching.html"Enabling API Caching to Enhance Responsiveness.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable API caching in Amazon ElastiCache.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot configure API caching in ElastiCache. You can use ElastiCache to limit requests to the database. However, this solution does not limit the traffic to the endpoint./ppFor more information about caching with ElastiCache, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticache/index.html"Amazon ElastiCache Documentation.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnable an auto scaling group on the endpoint service and databases.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can configure an auto scaling group on the endpoint service and databases to help spread the load on the service. However, this configuration does not meet the requirement to reduce traffic to the endpoint./ppFor more information about auto scaling groups, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/auto-scaling-groups.html"Auto Scaling Groups.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an additional API Gateway and use an Application Load Balancer (ALB).
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You cannot scale API Gateway with ALB. API Gateway can handle any scale by itself./ppFor more information about API Gateway, see href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/welcome.html"What Is Amazon API Gateway?a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/welcome.html" /a

question_content: pA developer needs to create a serverless application that uses an event-driven architecture./p	pWhat should the developer do to implement the application's ability to receive and process events?/p/div

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Publish events to the queue. Create an SQS consumer on an Amazon EC2 instance that polls for new messages.
